articleTitle: Four-port Antenna Configuration in n78 5G Band for Energy Harvesting in Agricultural Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this paper, the authors have proposed a compact orthogonally arranged 4-port antenna configuration comprising series connected 3-element patch sub-array on each face having dimensions L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>×W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> (19.4 mm×22.32 mm) for Element1 and Element3 and L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>×W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (19.4 mm×26.32 mm) for Element 2 designed on commercially available FR4 substrate (ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> =4.3, tan δ =0.025). With respect to the center element (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>×W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), the sub array elements on its either side are equally and uniformly tapered so as to reduce the sidelobe level (SLL <-20dB) and the orthogonal arrangement of the 4-port configuration reduces mutual coupling (<-40 dB). The antenna system is suitable to work in the n78 (3.2-3.67 GHz) C band 5G having peak gain of around 6.55 dBi and radiation efficiency of about 35% having azimuthal angular width of 80° at the operating frequency 3.5 GHz. The configuration can thus be used to attain a precise 360° beam-steering aiding in energy harvesting for IoT based agricultural sensors.

articleTitle: Evaluation of alternative SKA-Low station layouts
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: A proposed alternative station layout (the “Vogel” layout) for the low-frequency 256 element Square Kilometre Array (SKA) is reviewed, and new embedded element pattern results are presented and discussed. It is noted that the Vogel configuration ameliorates previously noted issues with an earlier station layout, but that new antenna pattern issues are encountered at at a higher frequency band.

articleTitle: Differential Wilkinson Coupler with Reduced Reflections at Intersections
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper proposes a differential Wilkinson coupler operating from 105 to 145 GHz. In order to reduce the difference in transmission characteristics of a pair of differential signals, a Handshake structure is proposed to suppress the reflection of the crossing lines. The results of verification by electromagnetic field simulation show that the differential Wilkinson coupler with the Handshake structure has good characteristics.

articleTitle: Toward Electronically Reconfigurable Rims for Reflectors in Radio Astronomy
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper presents full-wave simulation results of a reflector-reflectarray hybrid antenna used as a spatial beamformer for mitigating interference in radio astronomy applications. Such antennas employ fixed reflectors with electronically tunable reflectarray along their rim to dynamically form nulls in the direction(s) of interferer(s). Results from realistic models of such antenas demonstrate their potential in producing nulls and potentially effectiveness in mitigating interference from satellites with the field of view of the instrument.

articleTitle: Stationarity Evaluation of High-mobility sub-6 GHz and mmWave non-WSSUS Channels
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Analysis and modeling of wireless communication systems are dependent on the validity of the wide-sense stationarity uncorrelated scattering (WSSUS) assumption. However, in high-mobility scenarios, the WSSUS assumption is approximately fulfilled just over a short time period. This paper focuses on the stationarity evaluation of high-mobility multi-band channels. We evaluate the stationarity time, the time over which WSSUS is fulfilled approximately. The investigation is performed over real, measured high-mobility channels for two frequency bands, 2.55 and 25.5 GHz. Furthermore, we demonstrate the influence of the user velocity on the stationarity time. We show that the stationarity time decreases with increased relative velocity between the transmitter and the receiver. Furthermore, we show the similarity of the stationarity regions between sub-6 GHz and mmWave channels. Finally, we demonstrate that the sub-6 GHz channels are characterized by longer stationarity time.

articleTitle: RF Electromagnetic Fields Exposure Monitoring using Drive Test and Sensors in a French City
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper presents the monitoring work on radiofrequency (RF) electromagnetic field (EMF) exposure, carried out in a French city by using drive test and sensor network methods. The drive test measurements are realized by continuously measuring in a car via a portable spectrum analyzer, i.e., Tektronix RSA 306B, connected to a 3-axis antenna. It records electric (E) field values over a broad cellular band (700 MHz – 3.8 GHz) along the pre-defined outdoor routes at a height of 2 meters above the soil level. Secondly, a total of 19 sensors are installed near the center of the city, on the streetlamps (4 meters to the soil), which measure the broad band (250 kHz – 6 GHz) exposure level. The statistical distribution of measurement data is analyzed, and compared with base station antenna (BSA) information, which can be publicly accessed. Furthermore, the temporal variation of measurements collected by sensor networks is analyzed.

articleTitle: Programmable Metasurface-Based Wideband Antenna for High-Gain Beam-Steering and Pattern-Reconfigurability Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: An electronically pattern reconfigurable metasurfaced antenna is presented in this paper. The proposed work comprises of a wideband monopole antenna and a single layered metasurface that act as a reflector. The metasurface consists of 16 independent reconfigurable elements that controls the radiation behavior of the antenna. Each element is triggered-On using a controlled DC source using microcontroller. The proposed configuration offers multiple radiation pattern starting from omni-directional to broadside, single to dual beam along with steering in both azimuthal and elevation plane. The −10dB impedance bandwidth of the antenna ranges 4 –8 GHz, while the metasurface loaded antenna offers a gain ranges 3 – 8dBi, depending upon the switching state of the programable metasurface. Owing the benefits of low profile and cost effectiveness the proposed antenna can be used for pattern diverse applications where high gain is required.

articleTitle: Complex-Source Beam Representation of the Fields Radiated by a Gaussian Window
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Frame based decomposition of fields provides a rigorous, flexible and effective tool to represent planar source field distributions as summations of Gaussian windows. The field radiated by each window can be approximated as a Gaussian beam in its paraxial region. In this context, beam shooting and bouncing techniques have been proposed as an alternative to corresponding ray methods for describing wave propagation in complex environments. Complex-Source beams, which are closely related to Gaussian beams, provide rigorous solutions for several canonical problems. The objective of this paper is to investigate relations between Gaussian beams radiated by frame windows and Complex-Source beams. Such an approach would open the door to extending the applicability of frame decomposition methods, enhancing Gaussian beam shooting by means of solutions provided by Complex-Source beams.

articleTitle: Continuous Phase Modulations for Sub-THz Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: We present the first experimental demonstration of a photonic-enabled wireless link using Continuous Phase Modulation in the sub-terahertz (sub-THz) frequency range. A carrier of 90 GHz is photonically generated and modulated by a 2.5Gbit/s signal with spectral efficiency of 1 (bit/s)/Hz. The receiver is placed at a distance up to 1.80 m and relies on an electronic approach.

articleTitle: Ionospheric Tomography Model Driven by Dynamic Measured Data and Its Multi-GNSS Verification
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Ionospheric electron density monitoring is of great significance for positioning and navigation, communication technology and space weather research. The improved tomography (DCS-PCA) method is proposed in this paper based on the compressive sensing fusion data-driven tomography (CS-PCA) method. The improved method can obtain real-time actual ionospheric characteristics by adding a dynamic measured tomography data-driven module to the CSPCA method, so DCS-PCA is more suitable for monitoring the active ionosphere than CS-PCA. The multi-GNSS observation collected from the ground-based system built by Qianxun Spatial Intelligence Inc. are used during the scintillation period in Hainan, the four-dimensional electron density models are constructed. By the dSTEC analysis of the independent reference station, it is found that the accuracy of the DCS-PCA model is significantly improved compared with the CS-PCA method, and the RMSE of ddSTEC on the GPS system is reduced by nearly 0.2. TECU (TEC Unit). The DCS-PCA method can effectively reconstruct the four-dimensional electron density of the active ionosphere, and plays an important role in the ionospheric monitoring and high-precision positioning.

articleTitle: Commissioning Observations in 2022 with 100-GHz MKID Camera at Nobeyama 45-m Telescope
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The observations at the 100 GHz frequency band evaluate thermal dust radiations and free-free emission characteristics of star-formation regions in the Milky Way. In our collaboration, the continuum camera with microwave kinetic inductance detector (MKIDs) is being developed for sub-millimeter astronomy. MKID is a resonator-based superconducting detector having an intrinsic potential to get over 1,000 pixels in one readout line. This large number of pixels can realize high sensitivity and wide sky coverage to observe detailed structures of astronomical objects. The camera with 109 MKID pixels for the 100-GHz frequency band was installed at the Nobeyama 45-m telescope in 2021. After the success of MKID performance evaluation with commissioning planet observations, several observations of star-formation regions (W49 and W51) and a quasar of 3C273 were performed in 2022. This report shows the overview of our instruments installed in the Nobeyama 45-m telescope with their performances and preliminary observational results in 2022.

articleTitle: A Proposed Radio Environment Monitoring System of Ali Observatory
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: With its extremely dry air and high altitude above 5000 meters, the Ail Observatory located in the Tibet plateau has been a promising site for several astronomical instruments working in the optical or millimeter wave bands. In addition to protect the dark sky around the Ali Observatory, the measures to protect local radio environment have also been discussed. Based on the requirements of radio astronomical instruments, a radio environment monitoring system has been proposed. This paper describes the preliminary design of the system, including the technical specification and the system composition. In the near future, this system will be put into use.

articleTitle: SnO2-based sensor for H2S detection in exhaled human breath
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this paper, the tin dioxide (SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>)-based thin film sensor for hydrogen sulfide (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S) detection in the frequency range is presented. The developed gas sensors were tested under exposure to the target gas (i.e.) H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S and interfering VOCs and NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in the ppm range at various temperatures (0-200°C). The sensor response (S) was defined as R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>/R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">air</inf>, where R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> is the electrical resistance in target gas, and R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">air</inf> is the electrical resistance in synthetic air. The highest responses were obtained for samples with 100 nm, measured at 150°C, in the 1-10 kHz range.

articleTitle: EMF exposure assessment through an online application: time and frequency domain data acquisition and processing
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: WebNir (https://webnir.eu) [1] is an open-access web platform that exposes several applications related to the assessment of risk from exposure to electromagnetic fields (EMF) are made available. This platform is developed by the "Nello Carrara" Applied Physics Institute of the National Research Council (IFAC-CNR) within the framework of a research project financed by INAIL (Italian Workers Compensation Authority). This paper describes the application that allows the automated processing of measurements produced by various instrumental chains operating in the time or frequency domain. The goal of these automated procedures is to perform the verification of compliance with exposure values, the calculation of various radiological protection indices and the graphical display of the source data and processing results. Initially, the procedure refers to the most common measuring instruments, implementing specific scanning algorithms for each. Then, this approach was extended to accept more generical measurement results, potentially produced by any measurement chain, as long as they are in open format (text file or spreadsheet). In particular, for data files whose structure is unknown to the system, the user provides the import procedure with the parameters necessary for its correct interpretation. The application also allows the calculation and representation of quantities not made available by the considered measurement chain (e.g., exposure indices, $\Delta \mathrm{B} /3\mathrm{s}$ variation).

articleTitle: Possible differences in exposure from TMS treatment between male and female operators
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper aims to evaluate the electromagnetic field exposure of a clinical operator performing a treatment protocol of Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) on a patient, by means of numerical dosimetry. In particular, the possibility that some differences could occur depending on the gender of the operator is raised, thus pointing out that a risk assessment gender-dependent may be relevant.

articleTitle: Complex-domain Pulse-wave Synchronous Feature Extraction For Millimeter-wave Adaptive Glucose Concentration Estimation: Proposal and Preliminary Experiments
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Millimeter-wave glucose concentration estimation is a promising technique for non-invasive glucose monitoring. However, the accuracy and stability are not high enough for practical use. For extracting blood signals stably, this paper proposes complex-domain pulse-wave synchronous (CPS) feature extraction to mitigate the effects of skin-condition fluctuation and measuring-point displacement. We measure scattering parameters in a frequency range of 60 - 80 GHz. Experimental results with invasive-measurement references show the effectiveness of our proposal, suggesting a possibility for realizing non-invasive blood glucose concentration estimation.

articleTitle: Calibration of an optically isolated GNSS Traveling Calibrator
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This article presents a global navigation satellite system (GNSS) Traveling Calibrator (TC) that transmits timing signals and feedback control signals over single mode optical fibre. The TC is a radio quiet instrument which emits very low radio frequencies. The main function of the TC is to calibrate GNSS receiver to antenna links based at radio telescopes that require minimum radio frequency emissions such as the MeerKAT radio telescope in South Africa. The TC was deployed at the MeerKAT site and calibrated using a MeerKAT global point positioning (GPS) station. A tailor-made proportional integral (PI) control system maintained the temperature of the TC within ±0.3°C from the set point over a 5 day observation period. The TC calibration values for the Pl and P2 codes were found to be 55.25ns and 54.90ns.

articleTitle: Design of Inter-satellite Ranging and Clock Synchronization of Formation Satellites
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Inter-satellite communication, ranging and clock synchronization (CRS) is a key technology for formation satellites to fly in formation and conduct distributed detection. The CRS system is based on the principle of dual one way ranging (DOWR) measurement, its hardware design and software design are described. In hardware design, frequency division multiplexing technology (FDM) is adopted to realize the communication among the formation satellites. Closed-loop clock discipline technology is conducted to realize clock synchronization among formation satellites. The CRS design is verified by series ground tests including wired ranging test on the desk, wireless ranging test in a microwave anechoic chamber, and wireless ranging test with a vehicle. The test data reveals the feasibility and effectiveness of the CRS design in this paper.

articleTitle: Efficient Implementation of the Vector-Valued Kernel Ridge Regression for the Parametric Modeling of the Frequency-Response of a High-Speed Link
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient implementation of the vector-output kernel Ridge regression (KRR). The proposed approach is applied to model the frequency-domain behavior of the magnitude of the transfer function of a parametric high-speed link as function of 11 parameters. The accuracy and the computational cost of the proposed technique are assessed on noisy samples and compared with the ones of a state-of-the-art modeling technique based on the combination of the principal components analysis (PCA) and the least-squares support vector machine (LS-SVM) regression.

articleTitle: A Method for Measuring Signals from 0.001Hz to 1Hz
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Ultra-low frequency signal measurements are required in deep space exploration. This paper presents a sampling algorithm to shorten the measurement time of ULF voltage by the time compression method. It is verified that the measurement result of 0.001Hz voltage can be obtained in 550s with an accuracy of 0.01%. The algorithm is also suitable for AC voltage measurements in the range of 1mHz to 1Hz.

articleTitle: Miniaturised Four-Electrode Conductivity Probe with PEDOT:PSS Coating
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper presents a miniaturized four-electrode probe for measuring the conductivity of biological tissues at radio frequencies. The probe was developed to address two common challenges in tissue conductivity measurements at radio frequencies: the limited size of the sample compared to the sensing volume of the probe and the electrode polarization effect. Measurement of the conductivity of the samples can be made by miniaturizing the probe so the sensing volume is smaller the size of the sample. To address the issue of electrode polarization, a PEDOT:PSS coating was applied on the electrodes to reduce the impedance of the electrodes, moving the polarization effect to lower frequencies outside the frequency range of interest. The results demonstrate that this miniaturized probe is a reliable and accurate tool for measuring conductivity of biological tissues at radio frequencies.

articleTitle: Automated Test Setup for Capacitive Power Transfer Coupler Impedance Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Capacitive power transfer is an emerging technology of which some parameters have not yet been sufficiently investigated. This article proposes an automated test setup to experimentally determine the key parameters, such as capacitance and leakage resistance, of a capacitive power transfer coupler. Using the results, the potential of capacitive power transfer in terms of, for instance, transferable power for a given distance, are revealed and theoretic models can be validated. An exemplary experiment shows that 5 mm plexiglass has a seven times greater leakage resistance than a 5 mm air gap.

articleTitle: 3D Joint Inversion of Multi-physics Data Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Joint inversion of multi-physics data can reduce inversion uncertainties and improve resolution. In this abstract, an efficient approach is proposed for 3Djoint inversion using a deep learning network to generate initial models for individual inversions. A two-round iteration strategy is adopted to improve the reasonability of the recovered models and the overall efficiency of the inversion scheme. Experiments demonstrate that our method can achieve higher accuracy and efficiency, compared to individual inversions and cross-gradient-based joint inversion.

articleTitle: Optimal Electrical Parameters of Deterministic Wireless Channel Prediction Models in Indoor Environment Based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Wireless channel prediction model based on ray tracking algorithm has been more and more widely studied and applied in indoor environment. However, the acquisition of environmental electrical parameters required by this method is inconvenient and costly. In order to solve this problem, this paper proposes a genetic algorithm based on a small amount of measured data to solve the optimal environmental electrical parameters corresponding to deterministic wireless channel prediction. Simulation results and measured results show that this method effectively improves the prediction accuracy of the infinite channel prediction model.

articleTitle: Status of a C-band Phased Array Feed with RFSoC digital beamformer
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this paper, we describe the design and development status of a room-temperature C-band Phased Array Feed (PAF) demonstrator, based on Radio Frequency System-on-Chip (RFSoC) for radio astronomy application, to be installed on the Sardinia Radio Telescope. The instrument is optimized to work across the 4.75-6.00 GHz radio frequency (RF) band. The project of the front-end includes a compact RF module based on an 8×8 array of linear dual-polarization antenna elements integrated with Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) Low Noise Amplifiers (LNAs). In the preliminary version of the front-end project, which considers only one linear polarization, a subset of 32 elements are connected to the LNAs, while the rest of them are terminated to 50 Ohm matched loads. A dedicated signal acquisition chain of microwave components, based on two stages of filtering and signal conditioning, permits the injection of the 32 RF signals to the two commercial back-ends based on RFSoC digital boards. Each board is equipped with 16 inputs, with 1.25 GHz instantaneous bandwidth, and performs the frequency channelization, the partial and final beamforming of at least four independent beams (the number of beams may vary depending on the observation requirements). A general description of the front-end design, the back-end hardware, firmware and software development and an optimizer for the whole system performances evaluation, is presented.

articleTitle: Low-Profile MIMO Antenna System for Vehicular Wi-Fi 7 Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: A low-profile 2x2 MIMO antenna system for Wi-Fi 7 is proposed in this paper that can be used in the automotive industry. Due to its physical properties and RF performance, the design can be placed in hidden locations such as front side mirrors, and front dashboard to provide coverage inside and outside the vehicle or even integrated in a low-profile housing on the vehicle’s roof. The proposed design is based on Planar Inverted-F Antenna (PIFA) with unique slots across its plane to cover the 2.4GHz band (2400-2495MHz), 5GHz band (5150-5895MHz), and 6GHz band (5945-7125MHz). The MIMO system is simulated using HFSS software and the results are presented in terms of reflection coefficients, passive isolation, surface current distribution, combined radiation patterns, and ports radiated efficiencies. The design shows very good RF characteristics which makes it an excellent candidate to be used for vehicular Wi-Fi 7 to meet the requirements of wider channel bandwidth, higher throughput rates, and increased omnidirectional coverage area with minimal interference.

articleTitle: Improvement of Long-Term Stability of Phase Measurement in Electrooptic Field Visualization System for Antenna Measurement in 300-GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: We demonstrate the electrooptic measurement system with long-term phase measurement stability suitable for the high-gain antenna characterization at the 300-GHz band. The long-term phase drift has been canceled out and the standard deviation of the phase measurement has been reduced by a factor of 10, compared to the conventional EO measurement system.

articleTitle: Progress in the Design of the Atacama Large Aperture Submillimeter Telescope
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The Atacama Large Aperture Submillimeter Telescope (At-LAST) aims to be the premier next generation large diameter (50 meter) single dish observatory capable of observations across the millimeter/submillimeter spectrum, from 30 GHz to 1 THz. AtLAST will be sited in Chile at approximately 5100 meters above sea level, high in the Atacama Desert near Llano de Chajnantor. The novel rockingchair telescope design allows for a unprecedentedly wide field of view (FoV) of 1-2° diameter, a large receiver cabin housing six major instruments, and high structural stability during fast scanning operations (up to ~ 3° per second in azimuth). Here we describe the current status of, and expected outcomes for, the antenna design study, which will be completed in 2024.

articleTitle: X-Shaped Slot Antenna for Sub-6 GHz 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this paper, a slot antenna with wideband characteristics is newly designed and proposed for use in sub-6 local 5G band. The slot antenna is in the shape of X character. In this design, a microstrip line is electromagnetically coupled to the feeding point at the center portion of the slot antenna. A microstrip tapered line is used for impedance matching and connecting to the 50 $\Omega$ input port. Throughout this paper, the antenna characteristics are evaluated by using the Finite Element Method (FEM) in a commercial simulation software (EMPro). From simulation results, −10dB impedance bandwidth is obtained within 3.2 GHz to 5.1 GHz, which is about 1.9 GHz bandwidth and realized gain has a peak value of 11 dBi at 4.7 GHz.

articleTitle: Improved Location Accuracy of L-Band Interference Sources Through Multiple Observations on L1C Products of the SMOS Satellite
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The European Space Agency’s Soil Moisture and Ocean Salinity (SMOS) mission operates in the 1400-1427 MHz frequency band. The measurements of SMOS radiometer are perturbed by radio frequency interference (RFI) that jeopardize part of its scientific retrieval in certain areas of the World. In order to switch off the detected interference sources, cooperation with the national authorities is essential since they are in charge of managing the radio spectrum in each country. For efficient cooperation, it is necessary to provide as much information as possible from each source so as to find the interfering equipment in the field. The SMOS spatial resolution is 38 km in the center of its field of view and it is not sufficient to define a reasonable search area on the ground. This paper presents the processes we carry out using SMOS level 1C products to improve the geolocation precision of interfering sources.

articleTitle: Scattering from a half oblate spheroidal cavity with DPS and DNG layers illuminated by a magnetic dipole
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: A new exact solution to an electromagnetic scattering problem is provided for the following geometry: a half oblate two-layered spheroidal cavity filled with anti-isorefractive double positive (DPS) and double negative (DNG) materials with a circular opening surrounded by PEC walls. The source is an axially oriented magnetic dipole located on the axis of symmetry inside the cavity. Exact analytical expressions for the electric and magnetic fields are provided. These analytical results can be used to verify validity of the newly developed or existing numerical simulation solvers.

articleTitle: Urban Damage Mapping With Reconstructed Quad-Pol SAR Data From Dual-Pol SAR mode
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) has the advantage of all-day and all-weather work, which can obtain high-resolution radar images and polarimetric scattering matrix of the target. The dual polarimetric SAR can obtain a wider observation swath with lower energy budget than quad-pol SAR. In this paper, the pseudo quad-pol SAR data is reconstructed from dual polarization SAR data based on the proposed deep convolutional neural network. The urban damage level mapping index is established based on the co-polarization coherence pattern and the reconstructed quad-pol SAR data. The experiments have been conducted on the multi-temporal ALOS/PALSAR data from the March 11 Eastern Japan earthquake. Compared with the existing quad-pol SAR data reconstructed method, the proposed method has superior reconstruction performance. The quantitative experiment results indicate the proposed method can effectively achieve urban damage level mapping based on the dual polarization SAR data.

articleTitle: The Influence of the Radio Channel on Precision of Position Estimation of the User Terminal Using the NB-IoT Radio Interface
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In the article the method of user terminal position estimation using the broadcast signals transmitted in the downlink of the NB-IoT interface was presented, including the analysis of the radio channel influence on precision of position estimation as well as the eNodeB (Evolved Node B) synchronization. The practical ability to estimate the position in the test area has been verified in the laboratory conditions, using the reference signals with a variable signal-to-noise ratio and different radio channel profiles. Additionally, the method that allows increasing the precision of the terminal position estimation without the need of increasing the sampling frequency of the radio signal is presented.

articleTitle: Deep learning for ionogram parameters scaling at polar region ionosphere
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Ionosondes are most widely used instruments to obtain electron density profiles of ionosophere. Typically ionosondes operates with $\gt 15$ minutes time intervals that is enough to obtain regular parameters of the ionosphere, but insufficient to study small- and medium-scale traveling ionospheric disturbances and sporadic E layers. The key points for such studies are the increase of the ionosondes time resolution, as well as automation of ionogram scaling routine. In this study we show the results of implementation of deep learning for ionogram parameters scaling. We trained and tested a convolutional neural network on data of Sodankyla ionosonde at high latitude region. Our results show a close to human ability to recognise layers shape of F1, F2, E, 6 types of Es and scaling foF1, foF2, foE, foEs parameters.

articleTitle: Multipath Extraction and Cluster Identification from an Indoor Measurement at 300 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Owing to the unique attributes of the terahertz (THz) band (0.1-10 THz) adoption of millimeter and centimeter wave channel models to characterize THz communication seems unrealistic. In this context, a cluster-based channel model using multipath components extracted from measurement data can serve as a crucial step in understanding the propagation characteristics of THz signals. In cognizance of the prior fact, the current work uses the Subgrid CLEAN algorithm to extract the multipath components (MPCs) using the data from a measurement campaign conducted in a typical conference room at 300 GHz. The extracted MPCs were further clustered based on their temporal and spatial characteristics using the K-Power Means (KPM) technique. The effectiveness of the employed extraction technique is validated by comparing the extracted power spectrums (angle and delay) with the measured ones whereas the efficacy of the clustering algorithm is demonstrated by identifying the interacting objects (IOs) causing the same.

articleTitle: Applications of Deep Learning Algorithms for RFEH, WPT and SWIPT Systems: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Deep learning (DL) has gained vast popularity in the research community in the recent years. The implementation of various DL algorithms in Radio-frequency energy harvesting (RFEH), Wireless power transmission (WPT), and Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT), among other numerous electromagnetics applications, has been widely explored to minimize the design complexity. This review article highlights recent developments in DL applied to RFEH, WPT, and SWIPT systems. It aims to provide interested readers and practitioners with helpful insights on the efficacy and potentials of DL algorithms as computational tools.

articleTitle: 300-GHz-Band Power Combiner-Radiator Complex Designed for Arrayed Photomixers
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: We designed and assessed a power combiner-radiator complex for integration with 300-GHz-band arrayed photomixers. The device consists of a microstrip-line based combiner (Wilkinson combiner or a T-junction combiner) and a patch antenna. Simulation results show an increase of the radiated power by 2.54 dB with a Wilkinson combiner and 2.94 dB with a T-junction combiner in comparison to a conventional single port-fed device. The results further show realized directional gains of 4.85 dBi and 5.04 dBi for the complex based on a Wilkinson combiner and a T-junction combiner, respectively. Additionally, the Wilkinson combiner gives better return loss and isolation between the input ports than the T-junction combiner, while the T-junction combiner has a better radiation efficiency of 85% compared to 77% of the Wilkinson combiner.

articleTitle: ALMA Band 6v2 receiver development status
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: We report on the design of the ALMA “Band 6v2” Superconductor-Insulator-Superconductor (SIS) receiver, an upgraded version of the existing 211-275 GHz ALMA Band 6v1 receiver. The Band 6v2 receiver complies with the strategies defined in the ALMA Development Roadmap to 2030. Our goal is to deliver an improved production-level receiver based on (i) a new Cold Cartridge Assembly (CCA) with increased sensitivity over an expanded 4-16 GHz IF (Intermediate Frequency) band (420 GHz goal) and a modestly expanded 209-281 GHz RF (Radio Frequency) band, and (ii) a new low-noise local oscillator (the Warm Cartridge Assembly or WCA). The new Band 6v2 receiver will be backward-compatible with the current Band 6 receiver and will be able to be installed in the ALMA Front-End cryostat as a replacement for the existing units.

articleTitle: Tropospheric Propagation Modeling for Opportunistic Rain Sensing using Current and Future Broadcast and Broadband Satellites
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Opportunistic rain sensing using satellite broadband and broadcast channels has recently proven to be a very accurate, cost-effective, and broad-coverage technique. Since it relies on accurate propagation channel modeling, it needs to keep the pace with the evolution of satellite-based communication systems, in particular in terms of the ever-increasing range of radio frequencies foreseen for the integration with (beyond-)5G networks. This paper performs a performance comparison between: i) a consolidated, though overly simplified, tropospheric channel model which was devised by the ITU for the design of Ku-band satellite broadcasting links, and ii) a more elaborate one, featuring two layers and best suited to fit higher frequency links. Numerical results using data collected by a satellite terminal show that the second model provides better results, especially in the case of low rain rates.

articleTitle: Innovations in LOFAR: An overview of improvements of the LOFAR telescope
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this contribution we describe recently implemented and upcoming improvements of the Low Frequency Array (LOFAR) radio telescope: The LOFAR2.0 upgrade, a redesign of the High Band Antenna electronics, and TMSS: LOFAR’s new specification and scheduling software that includes dynamic scheduling.

articleTitle: 3D-Printed Smooth-Walled Conical Horn Antennas: Manufacturing and Quasioptical Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Wireless power transfer systems may include focusing components to reduce spillover losses. In that case, the implementation of the theory of quasioptics assists in their optimization. This paper presents two 3D printed smooth-walled conical horn antennas used in one such system, at 5.8 GHz. This method results in a high performance, low-cost and lightweight antenna. This discussion includes the design, simulation, manufacturing and experimentation of the horns. Besides testing in an anechoic chamber for analysis of traditional antenna theory quantities, the electric field obtained through electromagnetic simulations is used to study the gaussian beam generated by the horns.

articleTitle: Long-distance and High-speed Underwater Optical Wireless Communication System ~Challenge to 1Gbps x 100m underwater optical wireless communication~
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper shows successful demonstration of underwater optical communication underwater optical wireless communication experiments at the transmission bitrate of 1 Gbps x transmission length of 100 m in the sea depth of 900 m off the coast of Sagami Bay using our developed equipment. We also evaluate optical transmission limits in underwater based on experimental results and theoretical optical attenuation in underwater.

articleTitle: A Far-Field Susceptibility Pattern of a Shielded Object
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this paper a susceptibility pattern of a shielded object is introduced. The pattern describes the amplitude response of the object (E-field response) to the excitation by the uniform plane wave of normalized amplitude and matched polarization within the full solid angle. The pattern visualization consists of three polar diagrams and is similar in concept to the intensity-polarization pattern used in optics and remote sensing. The proposed approach can be very useful in characterization of coupling paths through slots and apertures.

articleTitle: Radiofrequency Exposure Measurements on a 28 GHz Band 5G Base Station
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper presents the electromagnetic field (EMF) measurement results on a 5G frequency range 2 (FR2) base station (BS). In order to investigate the effect of measurement configurations (smartphone location and antenna type) and traffic load conditions on the EMF results, certain measurements are performed, and the results are analyzed and provided. It is found that the maximum instantaneous electric-field (E-field) strengths are only related to the measurement configuration and are not dependent on the traffic condition. However, the root mean square (RMS) E-field strengths rely on both the measurement configuration and the traffic condition. The RMS E-field strength differences between traffic on case and traffic off case are $\ge 19$ dB.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Antenna Design for Polarization-Insensitive Up-link Power Transmission and Down-link Harmonic Backscatters
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: To qualify requirements of polarization-insensitive up-link power transmission and down-link harmonic backscatters, dual-band dual-polarized antenna was designed, fabricated and measured, which achieves excellent gains of radiation patterns and isolation between horizontal (HP) and vertical (VP) polarizations within dual bands of $\omega_{0}$ and 2$\omega_{0}$($\omega_{0}=2.45$ GHz) by sharing identical physical antenna aperture.

articleTitle: Interplanetary Shock Three-Dimensional Tomography Based on Small Satellites
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The propagation mechanism, observation, and modeling of interplanetary coronal mass ejections (CMEs) are the main challenges for space weather forecasting. The interplanetary shock low frequency radio interferometer with small satellites program is proposed. Small satellites carry the low frequency interferometer and spectrometer, and formation flying in the sun-synchronous earth orbit with 1000km height, to from an interference array which the virtual aperture is about 100 km. Based on the characteristic of the frequency drift of radio type II bursts, the interference array will take three-dimensional tomography for interplanetary shock on sun-to-earth direction from 0.1MHz-30MHz. The program will provide key information on particle acceleration mechanisms associated with CMEs and help scientists forecast space weather on sun-to-earth propagation. Eight daughter microsatellites fly around the mother satellites. GNSS differential positioning and clock synchronization are used to determine the intersatellite interferometric vectors between the mother satellite and daughter satellites. The weight of each small satellite is about 50kg.

articleTitle: Novel C-shaped loop rectenna arrays for LED accessories
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Although microwaves leaking from a microwave oven can be converted into energy to light up the LEDs of resin accessories, it was difficult to light multiple LEDs at the same time. On the other hand, if the half-wave element of the Yagi-Uda antenna is changed to a loop-type element, the effect of waveguiding to the loop-type element is produced. However, if this is used as a rectenna, the LED will not light up because the rectifier circuit will be short-circuited. To overcome the issues, the novel C-type loop rectenna array with open loop elements is proposed. Based on the analysis, we made a prototype and succeeded in lighting multiple LEDs at the same time by arraying this rectenna.

articleTitle: MmWave Indoor Human Blockage Measurements and Modeling at 26, 62, and 70 GHz Bands
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper investigates the shadowing loss of the human body at multiple millimeter wave (mmWave) bands by real-time channel measurements and theoretical modelling. The human blockage (HB) measurements are performed at three frequency bands from 24 GHz to 73 GHz, in an open office environment set-up with computer clusters, using custom-designed Durham University’s channel sounder. Different blockage models are applied to simulate the human body shadowing (HBS) attenuation effects. The measurement and modeling results of this study are significant in terms of predicting the HBS attenuation for future network system applications.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of Forward and Inverse Solvers for Metasurface Design
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Electromagnetic forward and inverse solvers are considered for the analysis and design of electromagnetic metasur-faces. This paper reviews (i) a forward solver that takes the surface susceptibilities of metasurfaces and calculates their scattered fields and (ii) an inverse solver that takes user-defined desired power patterns and outputs the required metasurface properties. An omega-bianisotropic transmitting metasurface is then fabricated and measured to evaluate the performance of these forward and inverse solvers.

articleTitle: Deep supervised hashing for fast retrieval of radio image cubes
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The shear number of sources that will be detected by next-generation radio surveys will be astronomical, which will result in serendipitous discoveries. Data-dependent deep hashing algorithms have been shown to be efficient at image retrieval tasks in the fields of computer vision and multimedia. However, there are limited applications of these methodologies in the field of astronomy. In this work, we utilize deep hashing to rapidly search for similar images in a large database. The experiment uses a balanced dataset of 2708 samples consisting of four classes: Compact, FRI, FRII, and Bent. The performance of the method was evaluated using the mean average precision (mAP) metric where a precision of $88.5\%$ was achieved. The experimental results demonstrate the capability to search and retrieve similar radio images efficiently and at scale. The retrieval is based on the Hamming distance between the binary hash of the query image and those of the reference images in the database.

articleTitle: Aperture efficiency of beamforming with mutual coupling in SKA-Low stations
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Stations of SKA-Low comprise 256 antennas acting as an aperture array, with the primary output being a beamformed voltage datastream focused at a target object on the sky. The beamforming process applies geometric correction terms based on the layout of the station. Mutual coupling between antennas can generate direction dependent amplitude and phase perturbations for each antenna, violating the simplifying assumption that antenna element patterns are identical. This effect is analogous to surface imperfections in a dish antenna, and impacts the aperture efficiency. In this paper we use state-of-the-art Full Embedded Element (FEE) electromagnetic simulations of two candidate station lay-outs (pseudo-random and so-called “Vogel”) and calculate the statistical properties of the beamforming process for astronomical targets at several declination and over a wide range of frequencies. We use the statistics of FEE-induced phase variability to quantify the aperture efficiency as a function of frequency. The results show that the Vogel lay-out has lower phase variance at frequencies below approximately 125 MHz and generally the aperture efficiency is better than 90%, however the results depend on the source declination.

articleTitle: Maximum Permissible Transmission Line Loss to Meet a Target Gain for a Corporate-Fed Uniform Rectangular Array
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Very low-loss transmission lines are often required at millimetre wavelengths in order to meet performance targets. Using printed circuit board technology, extremely low-loss transmission lines are often more expensive and riskier than standard options. The ability to determine the maximum permissible transmission line loss allows designers to choose potential transmission line structures, thereby helping make this critical design choice. These results establish the maximum permissible transmission line loss in order to meet a target gain of a corporate-fed antenna array for a given the average active element gain and power divider excess loss.

articleTitle: VHF emitting width and 3D polarization of lightning dart leaders
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: After the lightning initial stage, lightning flash plasma channels (leaders) can become unstable and exhibit current pulses called dart leaders that propagate back down the lightning channel. These pulses are difficult to understand as they are a type of dielectric breakdown on an already existing plasma channel. In this work we present VHF radio observations (30-80 MHz) of three dart leaders with the LOFAR radio telescope with meter and nanosecond level accuracy. We show that the radio emission comes from a meter-level (or smaller) width core. We also present the first 3D polarization data of dart leaders which shows that, at least sometimes, the VHF currents in dart leaders are parallel to the leader channel. Together, these observations reveal that the primary streamer activity in a dart leader comes from a very thin region and does not significantly involve the corona sheath that was originally established by streamers.

articleTitle: Noise Figure Measurement of 60 GHz Band Amplifiers at Cryogenic Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper presents the measurement results of noise figure of 60 GHz band amplifiers at cryogenic temperatures. The amplifiers are monolithic microwave integrated circuits with CMOS FETs and GaAs MESFETs operating 60 GHz band. The noise figure is measured by the cold-source method using the vector network analyzer, when the amplifiers are cryogenically cooled by the cryostat. The noise figures of 60 GHz band CMOS and GaAs amplifiers can respectively reduce about 2.5 dB/100 K and 2 dB/ 100K until 150 K at 60 GHz. This paper concludes the usefulness of cryogenically cooled amplifier for 5G and 6G mobile communication systems.

articleTitle: Scattering power decomposition of dual-polarization SAR data: application to PALSAR-2 and Sentinel-1 data
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Scattering power decomposition method for polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data was extended to dualpolarization data in the previous study. The extended method was demonstrated an applicability to L-band SAR dual-polarization data. In this study, this method is applied to not only L-band but also C-band SAR dual-polarization data and evaluated the scattering mechanism caused by the different frequency SAR.

articleTitle: Impact of Sampling Frequency on the Performance of DEVIN: A personal EM UL Exposimeter
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: DEVIN is a miniaturized personal electromagnetic (EM) exposimeter that allows recording powers emitted by the mobile phone as well as identifying the user activities along the day. It is simply a hardware integrated into the shell of the smartphone. In the context of epidemiological studies, DEVIN is required to collect data from volunteers over a long period of time, e.g., a week. This implies a critical challenge related to the autonomy of its battery, which should be charged once per day. One solution to extend the battery autonomy consists on decreasing the sampling frequency. Therefore we intend in the present work to evaluate the performance of DEVIN at two different sampling frequencies for two various signals types, i.e., voice over LTE (VoLTE) and data uploading signals.

articleTitle: Theoretical Error Equation for FOA Based Localization by a Single Moving Observation Platform Considering Orbital Error
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze a method of localizing an unknown emitter by observing a sequence of Frequency Of Arrival (FOA) using a single moving observation platform, as shown in Figure 1. In particular, we consider the position and velocity errors of the moving observation platform into the theoretical localization error equation, which enables us to analyze the effect of these errors on localization accuracy without Monte Carlo simulations.

articleTitle: Feasibility of a Swarm-based proxy for amplitude scintillation on GNSS signals
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: We report about the early implementation of a Swarm-based S4 index which models the amplitude scintillation strength on Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals recorded at ground level. We leverage: (i) the plasma density data provided by the high-resolution faceplate measurements at a 16 Hz sampling rate made by the Electric Field Instrument (EFI) onboard Swarm satellites; (ii) Rino’s theory for weak scattering regime, which adopts a power law phase screen to enable modelling of amplitude scintillations; and (iii) the reconstruction of the irregularity layer based on the application of the NeQuick2 model, in a data ingestion scheme. This procedure is inspired by the Wernik-Alfonsi-Materassi (WAM) scintillation model approach for high-latitudes and for low-latitudes. The plasma density estimates made by Swarm are used to reconstruct the one-dimensional spectral slope p of the power spectrum of the plasma density irregularities measured in situ. The 16 Hz sampling rate, combined with the Swarm orbital features, allow modelling the effect of spatial scales having a typical scale size of about 500 m along the Swarm flight direction (roughly North-South), which causes L-band scintillations and affect the quality of GNSS-based positioning. The use of the Swarm-based proxy for S4 is potentially of great use for the community involved in studying, monitoring, and modelling the impact of small-scale irregularities on GNSS signals in the space weather context as it complements and extends the information based on ground-based observations, also by covering ionospheric sectors scarcely covered by ground scintillation data, including remote areas and over the oceans, being not easily accessible. We report about its formulation and early validation against S4 data from L-band Ionospheric Scintillation Monitor Receivers.

articleTitle: Research on the Coupling Mechanism of Creeping Waves Based on the Complex Planar Mesh Model
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In contrast to simple targets, high-frequency modeling of electromagnetic scattering from complex targets with surface diffraction requires consideration of the coupled propagation mechanisms and processes of reflection-creeping waves or creeping waves-reflection. And to solve the problem of accurate computation of trajectories and fields of coupled propagating rays, which is one of the technical bottlenecks limiting the wide range of applications of the theory of surface diffraction. To this end, in this paper, we propose a ray-path determination method for the coupling between creeping and reflected waves. The field of the creeping waves coupling mechanism is accurately described and calculated by combining the uniform geometric theory of diffraction (UTD) and the physical optics (PO). The characteristics of the fields generated by the coupling effects are analyzed through several examples, and the radar target properties are greatly improved from the scattering center type point of view.

articleTitle: Calibration of Pi-SAR2 Polarimetric Observation Data Using ABCI
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The polarimetric observation data of Pi-SAR2, an airborne polarimetric synthetic aperture radar, are very valuable because of its high resolution, but it cannot be used effectively because the data are not well calibrated with respect to elevation. Therefore, we have calibrated the data according to the observation conditions. The Pi-SAR2 observation data are very large due to its high resolution and require sufficient computational resources to be calibrated. We utilized the AI Bridging Cloud Infrastructure (ABCI) to calculate them. This paper reports on the calibration and scattering power decomposition of the Pi-SAR2 observation data using the ABCI.

articleTitle: Improved Foreground Modelling for Bayesian 21 cm Power Spectrum Estimation with BayesEoR
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Estimating the power spectrum (PS) of the redshifted 21 cm signal from the Epoch of Reionization (EoR) has proven difficult due to the presence of bright astrophysical foregrounds (FGs). Existing techniques to mitigate FGs during PS estimation under-utilize the data and do not properly account for the covariance between the observed EoR and FG signals. We are developing a Bayesian framework, BayesEoR, that jointly models the instrument, FGs, and 21 cm signal and marginalizes over their uncertainties to enable extraction of statistically robust and unbiased estimates of the EoR PS. In this paper, we present a brief overview of our approach to Bayesian PS estimation and the results of a recent study in which we used BayesEoR to analyze a set of detailed simulations containing mock EoR and realistic FG signals. Due to computational constraints, the forward model of the instrument in BayesEoR, which involves application of the instrument primary beam in the image domain, is restricted to model a subset of the sky. We find that, when the sky emission outside of the modelled domain is downweighted by the beam at the level of the dynamic range between the EoR and FGs, BayesEoR can model visibilities which see the whole sky using only a subset of the sky. We also present several techniques that can be used to mitigate FG contamination during EoR PS estimation while ameliorating computational costs.

articleTitle: Weak Target Detection Within Sea Clutter Based on EMD Fractal Feature
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In order to improve the target detection performance within sea clutter under low signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR), this paper focuses on the empirical mode decomposition (EMD) fractal property of sea clutter and its application on weak target detection. Firstly, the radar signals are reconstructed by EMD algorithm to suppress the impact of noise. Then the autoregressive (AR) spectrum fractal property of the reconstructed signal is analyzed in detail and the EMD-AR Hurst exponent is extracted for target detection. Finally, from analysis of the real radar sea clutter datasets, the results demonstrate that the proposed method increase the target detection probability than the traditional constant false alarm rate (CFAR) method and the existing fractal-based method under a low SCR condition.

articleTitle: Implementation of Bidirectional High-Rate Underwater Acoustic Communication Systems for Fully Wireless-Controlled Remotely Operated Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The use of underwater equipment, including remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), is being considered in marine industries. As radio communication is difficult underwater, wired control is used in most cases. The achievement of wireless-controlled ROVs could increase the safety and efficiency of underwater work in many aspects. This paper describes the implementation of our developed high-speed acoustic communication modem, which is capable of bidirectional communication and can transmit video. We demonstrate video transmission and remote control via acoustic communication in actual sea areas using a ROV equipped with the modem.

articleTitle: A filtering strategy to improve the MUSIC-based approach performances
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this contribution, a strategy that potentially allows to enlarge the maximum number of distinguishable targets by the MUSIC is proposed. A numerical example shows the feasibility of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Frequency-Dependent Nonuniform Energy Absorption around Human Eyeballs for the Electromagnetic Waves of 5G Mobile Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Numerical analyses have been performed regarding the propagation and absorption of electromagnetic waves around human eyeballs for five frequencies of the 5G mobile communication system. A direct irradiation and an irradiation over a glass plate are investigated and the results are compared. It is shown that the energy absorption in human body tissues around eyeballs strongly depends on the frequencies and that the distribution of the energy absorption is highly nonuniform. The electromagnetic wave of low frequencies around 700MHz penetrates the human head but the absorbed energy around eyeballs is not very large. However, the electromagnetic waves of 1.5GHz and 2.5GHz are absorbed strongly around the eyeballs where the vitreous body is located. The high frequency electromagnetic wave of 28GHz is not even transmitted into human head and absorbed very little in the eyeballs but absorbed largely by the skin. A glass plate of 1 cm in thickness with no-loss was inserted between the irradiation source and the human head, and the effect on the absorption rate was compared. The results show that the glass plate does not only reduce the energy absorption, but even increases for some cases depending largely on frequencies.

articleTitle: Micro Area Intelligent Wireless Channel Power Measurement System
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In order to study the propagation characteristics of electromagnetic waves in the urban micro-cell scenario in the 5G frequency band, we built an intelligent wireless channel measurement system. By inputting the movement route for the movable intelligent car, the GPS module and the USRP power measurement module were installed to realize the Automatically move and measure the position information and power information. The actual measurement results show that the measurement system operates stably in the micro-cell environment, and the measurement results are relatively accurate by analyzing the measured line-of-sight and non-line-of-sight conditions. easy operation, low coupling, and high convenience provide a novel method for automatic measurement of wireless channels.

articleTitle: Array antenna position measurement of Chinese Meridian Project Phase II at Mingantu Observing Station
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Methods of measuring the array antenna position of the Meridian II Project at Mingantu Observing Station are discussed.

articleTitle: RFI detection using cross-polarization coherence for dual-and full-polarimetric Synthetic Aperture radar
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: We propose a method to detect Radio Frequency Interference (RFI) superimposed on synthetic a perture radar (SAR) images using interferometric coherence in both range time and range frequency domain. We assume that RFI contains both horizontally and vertically polarized components at SAR reception, and therefore, propose to detect RFI by calculating similarity of those two channels. The method was applied to actual satellite SAR data and achieved RFI-free images with low computational cost and few RFI components.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Time-varying Wideband Interference Suppression Algorithm via GPU
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Time-varying wide-band interference (WBI) may severely deteriorate the target detection performance of radar systems. Highly overlapped with target echoes in time and frequency domain, WBIs could hardly be mitigated by 1-dimensional (1-D) signal processing methods. To effectively suppress time-varying WBI, an interference mitigation method based on time-frequency (TF) 2-D interference detection is realized on graphics processing unit (GPU) device, in which there are three stages involved. Firstly, 1-D radar echoes are transformed into the 2-D TF domain using short-time Fourier transform (STFT). Then, a constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detector is introduced for WBI identification in the TF domain. After that, the detected interference is mitigated by the TF filter. Finally, the time domain purified signals can be obtained by inverse STFT. Considering the high computational complexity of the TF interference mitigation method, a GPU device is used to accelerate data processing. The experimental results show that the TF interference mitigation method via GPU could not only suppresses WBIs effectively, but also provides much higher data processing efficiency.

articleTitle: A Partial-Annular Directional Antenna with Simple Structure for Limited Space
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: A partial-annular directional antenna with wide bandwidth and high gain is proposed in this paper. The radiator is a simple partial-annular metal microstrip loaded with hexagonal patch, which is exited with coaxial cable. The ground is reduced to a rectangular patch with small area, which is required by the deployment. As the reflector, the circular Aluminum plate is λ/10 below the radiator to enhance the antenna gain and front-to-back ratio (FBR). The air gap between the semi-annular antenna and the reflector is also helpful for the improvement of impedance math. The simulation results show that the relative bandwidth of the proposed antenna is 46.6% (3.85 – 6.19 GHz), and the gain varies from 7.91 to 9.93 dBi. Due to the semi-annular strip structure and defected ground, the proposed antenna could be used for the limited deployment space, such as radio wave detection, terminal of mobile communication, and so on.

articleTitle: Sensitivity of Surface Temperatures towards Lightning over the Indian Subcontinent
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In the present study, it has been attempted to demonstrate the individual response of surface temperatures on lightning frequency and intensity over the landmass areas of Indian subcontinent using high resolution lightning observations and reanalysis datasets. It was observed that the Northwest and Northeast sectors of the Indian landmass experience contrasting meteorological conditions and hence further investigation was done over each region separately which in turn depicted a prominent agreement between surface temperature and the lightning properties. However, an in-depth seasonal investigation revealed a much stronger sensitivity of lightning extremes towards the surface temperature anomalies during the premonsoon season of the NW region due to its hot, dry and less polluted environment. This was later also validation during the month of April where the probability of experiencing triads with extreme lightning is found to be four times higher during the hotter surface conditions which thereby warrants the primary impact of surface temperatures on lightning.

articleTitle: Non-Foster-inspired Time-varying Matching of a Small Transmitting Dipole
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Broadband matching of a small transmitting dipole is a long-standing problem in the antenna community. It is well known that classical passive resonant matching is inherently constrained by very narrow bandwidth. On the other hand, there are active approaches such as non-Foster-based matching and the recently intensively studied time-varying-based matching. This contribution gives a brief overview of all these approaches and compares their advantages and disadvantages. In addition, a novel approach is proposed that mimics a stable two-element non-Foster-based broadband matching of a short transmitting dipole, using a time-varying approach.

articleTitle: Channel Impulse Response Measurements at mmWave Band in Office and Conference Rooms
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this paper, the measurements of the channel impulse response at mmWave band in office and conference rooms are described. The central frequency is 27 GHz with a bandwidth of 400 MHz. The description of the used measurement stand and considered environments are presented. The initial analysis of the power delay profile, mean delay, and RMS delay spread allows preliminary conclusions to be drawn that there is a significant impact of the dimensions of the rooms on these parameters.

articleTitle: Overview of Lightning Current Observation at Tokyo Skytree
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Direct observation of lightning current is a fundamental approach to evaluating lightning parameters, which are among the most basic factors for the lightning protection design of various grounded objects. However, for a tall grounded structure, upward lightning flashes initiated from the top of the structure have usually been observed, and the direct observation results of downward flashes have been limited. Tokyo Skytree is a free-standing independent broadcasting tower, which height is 634m-ASL, located on a flat terrain about 8 km inland in Tokyo, Japan (35.71°N, 139.81°E). The authors have conducted lightning current observation with the Rogowski coils at the tower since 2012. At Tokyo Skytree, we have confirmed 38 downward-initiated lightning flashes and 69 upward-initiated lightning flashes to the tower as of the end of December 2022 for 11 years. In this paper, we overview the lightning current observation and the recent result at Tokyo Skytree.

articleTitle: Multi-Function Digital Signal Processing System for a 110-meter Radio Telescope
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The QiTai radio Telescope (QTT) is under construction in northwest China. It will be equipped with multiple single-beam and Phased Array Feed (PAF) receivers to achieve continuous frequency coverage from 270 MHz to 30 GHz in the first stage. The receivers are located in separate places with different frequencies, bandwidths, and number of channels, which increases the design complexity of signal acquisition and transmission. The Ultra-WideBand (UWB) and PAF receivers will generate a large amount of data, and the signal processing algorithm for multi-object observation is complex and computational, which poses a great challenge to the data processing system. Based on the integrated, high-performance Radio Frequency System-on-Chip (RFSoC) technology, sampling the RF signals directly at the receiver front-end, a state-of-the-art and resource-shareable QTT signal acquisition and transmission scheme will be shown in this paper. To cope with the real-time processing of massive data, QTT will employ a multifunctional post-processing system based on High-Performance Computer clusters (HPC) that can handle a variety of scientific observation modes such as pulsars, transients, molecular lines, continuous and VLBI/baseband, etc. Many useful features such as Radio Frequency Interference (RFI) cancellation, commensal observation, and raw voltage data capture are also included in this system. The scalability of this heterogeneous architecture is excellent, and more channels or larger bandwidth receiver signals can be expended by increasing the number of RFSoC and HPC processing nodes.

articleTitle: Lightning Localization Using Three-Dimensional Time Reversal MUltiple SIgnal Classification (TR-MUSIC) Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this paper a three-dimensional (3D) Time Reversal MUltiple SIgnal Classification (TR-MUSIC) algorithm is proposed to localize lightning discharges. The performance of the proposed algorithm was evaluated considering different scenarios and taking into account the presence of noise.

articleTitle: LSTM-based In-band full-duplex NOMA-OFDM Receiver with Non-linear SI Estimation/Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this research, we aim to investigate Long Short Term Memory based SER performance in in-band full-duplex NOMA-OFDM receiver for detection of signal of interest from NOMA-OFDM multi users when both the weak user and strong user are present along with self-interference signal received at the receiving antenna from its own transmitting antenna of the base station operating in full-duplex mode under various channel imperfection. For this, we have proposed a three phase Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) based approach for canceling the non-linear self-interference in a full-duplex system and detecting the signal of interest. Extensive simulation studies show that the proposed LSTM-based method outperforms the existing deep learning as well as traditional MMSE-based methods.
