articleTitle: The Independence of AIMD Lead Transfer Functions on the Trajectory Shapes
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Numerical and experimental methods are used to understand the impact of trajectory variations on the active implantable medical device (AIMD) models, i.e., the transfer functions, used for RF-induced heating safety evaluation. The transfer function (TF) models are developed along various trajectories via numerical modeling and experimental measurements. Based on the trajectory used in this study, it was observed that the trajectory has little effect on TF. Consequently, the TF can be used to evaluate the RF-induced heating for various implantation trajectories inside human body models.

articleTitle: Fiber-based time transfer system for ngVLA system
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: For fiber-based time transfer systems [1, 2, 3], the transmission delay can be compensated by roundtrip delay measurement. For highly accurate transmission delay compensation, the delays in the forward and backward paths of the fiber must be identical. In this method, we should consider the chromatic dispersion effect. We’ve developed a fiber-based time transfer system with the same optical frequency on both paths. This time transfer system is highly compatible with the frequency transfer system we have already developed, and can share a single fiber.

articleTitle: How the upper atmosphere effects can influence European technological systems: a study of the socioeconomic quantification
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The new solar cycle and the increasing use of technological systems that make humans increasingly vulnerable to the effects of Space Weather have made the study of socioeconomic impacts in the upper atmosphere useful and necessary. This paper therefore aims to raise awareness among as many people as possible of the importance of quantifying the socio-economic impacts of Space Weather to calculate the costs associated with mitigation actions in the sectors most affected.

articleTitle: Error Analysis of Sommerfeld Integrals for Microstrip Antenna Problems
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Accuracy of computation for Sommerfeld integrals is examined for applications to microstrip geometries. In a numerical approach proposed earlier, the influence of the singularities in the integrand is obviated by deforming a small portion of the contour from the real axis to the 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> quadrant, thus avoiding the branch point and surface wave pole singularities in the $4^{\mathrm{t}\mathrm{h}}$ quadrant of the complex plane. The overall computational strategy comprises of numerical integration across the finite, deformed contour followed by a closedform evaluation of the tail part of the Sommerfeld integral. Given a specified a-priori error bound, a criterion for assessing the computational errors is developed here that restricts the maximum height of the deformed contour in the 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> quadrant. Preliminary numerical results included here suggest the validity of the method while also indicating that there is scope for augmenting this criterion for large values of lateral separations between the source and observation locations.

articleTitle: Dual Band MIMO Monopole Antenna System for 5G Laptops
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band multiple-input multiple-output(MIMO) monopole dual-antenna system for fifth-generation(5G) laptops. The dual-antenna unit is a $29 \times 2 \times 3$ mm $^{3}$ three-dimensional structure with two antennas of the same structure and size, consisting of a fed monopole and a shorted monopole. Dual antennas are arranged 4 mm apart, side by side, in the same direction, to form a dual antenna unit. This antenna system can cover 5G dual-band operation of 3300-3600MHz and 4800-5000MHz, and the measured antenna efficiencies can reach more than 40%, which is well suited for multiple antenna applications.

articleTitle: Suppression of Mainlobe Deceptive Jammers with SF-RDA Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of suppressing main-lobe deceptive jammers based on a novel stepped frequency (SF)-receive delay array (RDA) radar. In our system design, the linear frequency modulation waveform is transmitted with a SF across the transmit antenna elements, and the received echo is delayed with a time shift between adjacent receive elements. In this regard, the range-angle-dependent transmit and receive steering vectors are obtained, making it possible to distinguish the true target and the main-lobe deceptive jammers, especially those generated in the same transmit pulse behind the true target. Furthermore, a joint transmit-receive beamforming method is developed, including the data-independent transmit beamforming and the dimension-reduced data-dependent receive beamforming. Therefore, the jammers are suppressed by nulling in the joint transmit-receive spatial domain. Numerical simulations are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in suppressing mainlobe deceptive jammers.

articleTitle: Full-phase control millimetre wave metasurface element enabled by air-bridged Schottky diodes
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: A novel design of a full-phase control metasurface element using two independent controlled diodes in a millimetre wave frequency band is presented. By individually providing a reverse bias to two air-bridged Schottky diodes placed respectively on two split dipoles in a periodic unit cell, it is possible to control the capacitance and, therefore, the reflected phase of the metasurface. Importantly, a parasitic element coupling technique is used to achieve full phase control and improve the reflection losses. Simulations of the proposed design are presented. CST Microwave Studio was used to evaluate the tuning range and the reflection characteristics of the proposed design.

articleTitle: Generation of Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) by Metasurface Lens Antenna at 140GHz for 6G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this work, we demonstrate a novel design and analysis procedure of a meta-surface lens antenna that can generate arbitrary OAM mode. Given a unit-cell design and a custom phase profile on the antenna aperture, a metasurface lens antenna, or meta-lens in abbreviation, is automatically generated by a script. A full wave EM model analysis including a feed horn and the OAM meta-lens is then conducted to validate the desired vortex behaviors of corresponding OAM modes.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Wilkinson Coupler Under Different Input Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In sub-terahertz receivers, it is indispensable to apply beamforming that combines multiple RF paths from the viewpoint of SNR (signal to noise ratio) improvement by increasing the directivity of the communication path. For beamforming in the case of mm-wave band application, the receiver is placed near the antenna. However, in the case of sub-terahertz band application, where the wavelength is short, the RF paths must be directly synthesized because space for a receiver is not available. It is desirable to apply a Wilkinson Coupler composed of simple passive elements to combine RF paths. When applied to beamforming, the amplitudes and phases of signals to be combined may differ greatly. It is also necessary to turn off some input signals for calibration.In this case, it is difficult to fix the impedance in the OFF state to a specific impedance. For this reason, it is desirable to have low sensitivity to the impedance in the OFF state. In this paper, we analytically confirm that the Wilkinson Coupler can operate normally even in such a special situation.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Aided Beam Prediction in Dual-Band Multi-Cell Massive MIMO System
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Sub-6GHz and millimeter-wave (mmWave) are two primary frequency resources in the fifth-generation mobile communication technology (5G) and beyond. Their coordination permits higher reliability in a dual-band multi-cell massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system. However mmWave is extremely sensitive to multipath fading and interference under different communication scenarios for the poor penetration, thus making the beam prediction critical. In this paper, we propose a strategy to predict the mmWave beams through sub-6GHz channels without estimating channel state information (CSI). We first establish a dual-band multi-cell massive MIMO system model and formulate the problem by selecting beam vectors to maximize the transmission rate of the system. Since the essence of beam prediction is similar to supervised classification, we then construct a deep neural network (DNN) to explore the mapping relationship between sub-6GHz and mmWave channels based on their spatial correlation properties. The numerical results show that the proposed DNN can predict the mmWave beams with an accuracy of over 90%.

articleTitle: Challenges in the measurement at W band
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper presents the different problems we have encountered in the W-band radiation pattern measurements in the spherical system and the solutions we have implemented to solve them. The measurements have been made based on an 8-element slot array in different manufacturing technologies such as Electrical Discharge Machining(EDM) and 3D printing.

articleTitle: The variometric approach for the monitoring of natural hazard-induced ionospheric perturbations
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This work shows how the VARION (Variometric Approach for Real-Time Ionosphere Observation) algorithm, able to estimate the TEC variations in real-time, can be used to shed the light on the mechanism of Lithosphere-Atmosphere-Ionosphere Coupling (LAIC) and thus to be used for ionospheric monitoring of natural hazards events. In particular, we present the methodology of Total Variometric Approach (TVA) was developed to estimate the tsunami genesis and to support classic methods for tsunami warning system. TVA is based on the joint application of VADASE (Variometric Approach for Displacements Analysis Standalone Engine) and VARION to estimate ground shaking, co-seismic displacements and TEC disturbances, using the same real-time GNSS data stream. Furthermore, we present an oceanic-ionospheric joint analysis after the 2022 Tonga eruption. We report on the reversed amplitude of the two phenomena in the oceans and in the ionosphere. The sea-surface perturbation caused by the Lamb wave was not significant, while ionospheric perturbation was considerable. In contrast, the regular tsunami waves manuscript reached ~1m around New Caledonia-New Zealand and ~2m along the Chilean coastline; however, the associated ionospheric perturbation was quite small, half the size of the Lamb wave perturbation. We finally explore the possibility to increase the amount of available data for a denser ionospheric monitoring, applying VARION also to observations coming from geostationary satellites, from ship-based GNSS receivers and from smartphones.

articleTitle: Topology optimization of Optical and Millimeter-wave Circuit Devices Using Finite Element Method and Function Expansion Method
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: To develop optical and millimeter-wave circuit devices with desired transmission properties, various kinds of design optimization methods have been proposed so far. Among them, topology optimization, which can automatically generate device structures with arbitrary topology, is the most powerful design method. We have originally developed function-expansion-based topology optimization technique and have applied it to design of optical and millimeter-wave circuit devices. In this paper, we present this method in view of some practical aspects.

articleTitle: A Convex Optimized Estimator of the Laplacian Operator for Bioelectric Simulations
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Simulations of bioelectric potentials in the direct problem usually require numerical integration in the spatial dimensions to obtain both the transmembrane current diffusion and the extracellular potentials in homogeneous conductivity conditions. Given that the Laplacian of a potential field in said conditions is a spatially linear operator, we propose its implementation with non-uniformly spaced point clouds using a static-matrix formulation which avoids the integration in the spatial domain. We also analyzed the effect of severe irregular sampling in these calculations. Matrix estimators in the 3-dimensional space were built for the Laplacian operator in point clouds defining lines and surfaces. An optimized algorithm was proposed, in which the spatial convolution of the Laplacian impulse response is locally and globally estimated using convex programming techniques, sparse matrix representations, and basic concepts of Graph Theory. We benchmarked the behavior of the estimated synthetic transmembrane and extracellular potentials with simple geometrical substrates. Our proposal paves the way towards simplifying spatial evolution in computer simulations and its use in more clinically realistic environments, such as non-homogeneous conductivity in volume conductor problems and patient-based arrhythmia simulations from point clouds in Electrophysiology Laboratory.

articleTitle: Contactless Switching of a RF CBRAM Switch
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to wirelessly rewrite the CBRAM switches for chipless RFID tag IDs. The contactless driving of the CBRAM switch is achieved by inductive coupling between a writer coil and a tag coil. On the writer side, a voltage pulse is generated on a coil which induces a varying electromotive force across another coil which is connected to the CBRAM (device part). Numerical analysis and circuit simulations were performed to confirm that pulse waves are thus induced in the device coil and it allows to switch the CBRAM. In addition, experimental results showed that the CBRAM was successfully switched from the On state to the Off state by applying multiple pulses to the writer coil.

articleTitle: IGS Ionosphere Working Group cooperation with IRI – provision of GNSS TEC products to GAMBIT database
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The current activities of IGS Iono Working Group include several different fields of development which allows for rapid increase of product’s quality and usability. Great examples include the extension of ROTI maps to cover southern hemisphere and equatorial region in depiction of ionospheric irregularities as well as the development of real time GIMs. IGS Iono WG also directly cooperates with IRI group to provide the users with data fusion products allowing for thorough analysis of the ionosphere.

articleTitle: A Series-fed Patch Array Antenna for Bessel Beam Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: A dual port series-fed two-port microstrip linear ar- ray capable of generating Bessel beam is presented in this article. The array is amplitude and phase tapered to generate the desired Bessel beam along with the combiner action. The antenna when fed at the ports $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$ exhibits a parallel combiner action at the operating frequency with the generation of Bessel beam in the near field. A 16-element array designed at 2.4 GHz is simulated in a 3D EM solver for analysis. The obtained results indicate inherent combiner action along with Bessel beam generation. The dual-port combiner nature of the radiator makes the structure an excellent candidate for transmitter applications for multi-tone signals.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Quantification of Epithelial/Absorbed Power Density in 1-layered Planar Skin Model with Uncertain Tissue Electric Properties
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper presents a stochastic approach to compute the absorbed power density (APD) on skin surface when exposed to radiation of halfwave dipole antenna. Skin tissue is modelled as 1-layered half-space with uncertain electric permittivity and conductivity. Formulation is based on numerical solution of Pocklington equation and corresponding field integrals. Stochastic Collocation (SC) method is used for uncertainty propagation in a black box manner. APD mean, variance, skewness, kurtosis and confidence intervals are computed at 10, 30 and 90 GHz for different antenna-body distances.

articleTitle: A Multi-branch Deep Learning Architecture for Microwave-Ultrasound Breast Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: A novel deep convolutional fusion architecture with multiple branches is proposed to address the challenges posed by electromagnetic inverse scattering problems. Traditional inverse scattering techniques suffer from various difficulties, including strong ill-conditioning, high computational cost, and intrinsic nonlinearity. To overcome these challenges, a multi-branch convolutional neural network (CNN) is proposed for reconstructing two-dimensional (2D) images of breast permittivity in order to detect tumors. The proposed architecture, which is influenced by objective-function methods, inputs scattered-field data and ultrasound-derived breast mask as prior information to reconstruct images of permittivity. The architecture consists of two branches, a decoder-only branch and a convolutional branch, to handle inputs of different formats. The final reconstructed 2D image is obtained by fusing the outputs of these two branches. The CNN is trained using eight numerical MRI-based breast models. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach provides high-quality imaging for high-contrast objects of interest. This work opens up a new avenue for real-time quantitative microwave imaging using deep learning.

articleTitle: The MMwave Channel Sounder Based on Antenna in Module
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The Millimeter-wave (MMwave) and the beamforming technology havs been the key technology of 5G. To solve the difficulty of measuring the beamforming of MMwave and promote the application of the MMwave, this paper used the real example to offer a MMwave channel sounder solution with Antenna in Module (AiM). It describes the solution of AiM and the channel sounder. And give the test experiments of the channel sounder with AiM to prove the validity of the proposed solution.

articleTitle: Is Laplacian indispensable to Magnetic Resonance Electrical Property Tomography (MREPT)- An analysis from the perspective of Reconstruction Error Compensation Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Magnetic resonance electrical properties tomography (MREPT) is a promising technique for non-invasive, early cancer detection based on the electrical properties of tissues. However, noise sensitivity and artifact problems have historically hindered the clinical application of MREPT. In order to address these limitations, researchers have investigated several approaches, including data-driven neural network methods, modified analytical models, or a combination of both. However, these methods face the challenge of balancing the trade-off between reducing artifacts and maintaining tissue contrast in MREPT. This study presents an analysis of our proposed Reconstruction Error Compensation Neural Network (REC-NN) and provides new insights into the input features utilized in the model. Special focus was put on the Laplacian of the source signal for MREPT, which is the most important term in most analytical models, to make clear its role in REC-NN with regard to the shape, contrast and accuracy of the reconstructed conductivity map.

articleTitle: A Simulation Model for EMC Compliance Assessment of Induction Cooktops for Cardiac Implanted Electronic Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The increasing medical use of cardiac implanted electronic devices (CIEDs) for heart patients increases the risk of device malfunction or damage due to electromagnetic interference (EMI). In this work we focus on the EMI sources produced by induction cooktops operating at intermediate frequency (IF). A computational model is proposed to evaluate the induced voltage and the magnetic field in a pacemaker according to the ISO 14117 standard. The method is based on a finite element analysis (FEA) of the magnetic field configuration. A post-processing analysis was then performed with the approximated method to evaluate the maximum voltage induced in the standard-size loop of a pacing lead.

articleTitle: Equatorial Plasma Bubble Detection using the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Support Vector Machine (SVM)
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Equatorial plasma bubbles (EPB) refer to the area of low electron density in the Earth’s ionosphere near the equator during post sunset and post-midnight. They influence the radio communications and GPS signals. In this work, we study the EPB occurrences and characteristics using the VHF radar images observed at the Chumphon station, Thailand, near the magnetic equator.. We develop an EPB image detection system using a hybrid learning technique with convolutional neural network (CNN) and support vector machine (SVM) and evaluate the accuracy of the proposed CNN-SVM model using two kernels: polynomial kernel and radial basis function (RBF) kernel.

articleTitle: Rate region and Interference impact analysis for spectrum sharing in 6G NTN-TN networks
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The convergence of non-terrestrial networks (NTN) and terrestrial networks (TN) is crucial in achieving global coverage in the 5G/6G era. The 3GPP Rel-17 and ongoing Rel-18 NTN specifications are pushing for integrating satellite connections with cellular phones. However, as satellite services become more widespread, a spectrum shortage is expected to become a major issue. Spectrum sharing between satellite and cellular networks is considered a promising solution to overcome the spectrum shortage. However, a rigorous study of spectral efficiency and interference impact is necessary to justify the advantages of NTN-TN integration. This manuscript designs an experiment to investigate the spectral efficiency and interference impact of NTN-TN reverse pairing, a preliminary mitigation method of using BS transmission directivity. The simulation result through a 3GPP-calibrated simulator shows that spectrum sharing between NTN and most TN base stations (BS) could enhance spectral efficiency in the NTN-TN integrated network. On the other hand, network operators could configure dedicated radio resources for a few TN BSs with severe interference to protect NTN operations.

articleTitle: CO2 Raman scattering measurements in seawater for marine lidar
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Real-time measurement of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> Raman signals can aid in determining the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> concentration dissolved in the sea. We are developing a Raman lidar that can be installed into a drone for CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> monitoring in seawater. In this report, we present results of measuring CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> Raman signals dissolved in pure water and seawater using an Nd:YAG laser at a wavelength of 355 nm by using spectrometer and ICCD camera as basic experiments. We were able to detect CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> Raman signal could be detected up to 80 ppm when dissolved in pure water and 120 ppm when dissolved in seawater and found a correlation between CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas concentration and signal intensity. The measurement results suggest that both the intensity of Raman scattering changes linearly with respect to CO2 gas concentration from 80ppm to 1240ppm. We design the lidar configuration by considering this results of the fundamental experiment.

articleTitle: Reflective Intelligent Surfaces: Enabling Reconfigurability with Composite Vortices
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Enabling the reconfigurability of Reflective Intelligent Surfaces (RISs) is a challenging task that needs to be addressed for their full exploitation in a smart electromagnetic environment. Although different practical solutions have been proposed, they typically involve complex control systems, affecting the cost to produce, deploy, and operate RISs. As an alternative solution, we discuss the possibility of exploiting the topological properties of vortex modes for controlling in real-time the RIS response, allowing for a simpler practical implementation.

articleTitle: An Alternative Method to Identify the Susceptibility Threshold Level of Device under Test in a Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: By counting the number of pass/fail occurrences of a DUT (Device under Test) in the stirring process in a reverberation chamber (RC), the threshold electric field (E-field) level can be well estimated without tuning the input power and repeating the whole testing many times. The Monte-Carlo method is used to verify the results. Estimated values and uncertainties are given for Rayleigh distributed fields and for Rice distributed fields with different $K-$factors.

articleTitle: Modeling LTE MIMO Antenna Systems on Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper continues analyzing the performance of our previous work in [1] for 4x4, 4x2, and 2x2 LTE MIMO antenna systems. These systems were studied in Frankfurt, Germany which is an urban environment on a vehicle with metal and glass roof top for a virtual road around the city. The first part of this research paper shows the simulation results using FEKO software on vehicle that analyzes spatial and polarization diversity on Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC) for two quarter-wave monopoles operating at 2110 MHz. Next, the ECC is analyzed as a function of hemispherical coverage and angular resolution. The second part of this paper presents throughput results for a virtual route utilizing measured radiation patterns of MIMO architectures of 2x2, 4x2, and 4x4 on an SUV with metal roof and glass roof. The measured radiation patterns are imported to Altair’s WinProp software that can provide results for electromagnetic wave propagation inside the city on a virtual route and RF cellular network planning for base stations.

articleTitle: Near field positioning system based on anisotropic magneto resistive sensor for knee prosthesis
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this work, we present a near field magnetic system for knee orthopedic prosthesis positioning operating in LF band (100 kHz). The system can be used for every type of knee prosthesis provided they are made of metal. The current system made of a single emitting coil and three anisotropic magneto-resistive sensors allows to detect the femoral shield and is validated by practical measurement and simulations.

articleTitle: Deterministic-Stochastic Modeling of Current Diffusion Equation (CDE) for Plasma Confinement
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The paper deals with deterministic-stochastic modeling of the current diffusion equation (CDE). Deterministic part of the analysis is carried out by means of standard finite element method (FEM). Stochastic postprocessing of the deterministic results is carried out by means of nonintrusive stochastic collocation method (SCM) and analysis of variance (ANOVA) approach. Some numerical results illustrating the convergence of SCM, confidence interval and sensitivity indices are given in the paper.

articleTitle: Plasma Frequency Determination from In-situ Wave Receivers
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Plasma frequency is a fundamental parameter in the space plasma environment and is most accurately derived from in-situ wave receivers. Although semi-automated methodologies have been developed for use with post-processed data to extract the upper hybrid resonances from dynamic spectrograms, these such tools require significant attention from trained operators as a man-in-the-loop. Pattern recognition/image classification is an ideal technology to resolve such problem. Initial results from the signal identification algorithm developed at AFRL demonstrate its utility in solving an outstanding problem dating to the beginning of space age. Once proven successful, the fully automated application can be modified to provide space measurements as input for any assimilative model significantly improving predictive capabilities. Similar algorithms can be tailored to support future mission with similar wave receivers.

articleTitle: Observations and statistics of the plasmasphere boundaries from the Van Allen Probes
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: We deduce the cold electron plasma density from NASA Van Allen Probes measurements throughout 2012-2019. We then extract two of the plasmasphere boundaries. We first use the gradient method for locating the plasmapause at L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pp</inf> and, then, the $100\mathrm{~cm}^{-3}$ density threshold for the plasmasphere outer edge located at L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100</inf>. The sharp gradient of the plasmapause is only defined in 53% of cases, while L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100</inf> is defined for $\sim 85\%$ of cases. Differences and similarities between L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pp</inf> and L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100</inf> are discussed. L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100</inf> is demonstrated to bound the plasmasphere at large L-shell in the dusk where L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pp</inf> gradients often lack. We generate new empirical density models of the plasmasphere boundaries binned by L-shell, magnetic local time (MLT), and the maximum of the Kp index over 24 hours (Kp*).

articleTitle: Photonic Phase Stabilization for PSK Terahertz Wave Transmission
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Higher-frequency carriers are inevitable for higher-speed wireless communication. To maximize their advantage, phase stabilization is an essential technology for phaseshift-based multi-level modulation. At photomixing, which has been a promising way for continuous THz-wave generation, we have devised a Mach-Zehnder interferometric phase stabilization method. However, the serious drawback of the method is the ineffectiveness for a phase-modulated THz wave. This time, we invent a phase stabilization system with a backward-direction lightwave overlapping on the THz-wave generation system. A conceptual and experimental setup of phase detection and phase stabilization is presented in this paper. The stabilization system is revealed to be effective at above a couple of Gbit/s.

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Evaluation of the High-gain Antennas Based on the Electrooptic Near-field Measurements and Direct Far-field Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: We demonstrate that the far-field patterns of the high-gain antennas (about 50 dBi) obtained based on the near-field measurements using the electrooptic probe in the table-top system and the direct far-field measurements with the antenna separation of 13.5 m are in good agreement with each other. The results show that the near-field measurements based on photonics techniques using low-disturbance electrooptic probes will pave the way for the evaluation of high-gain antennas in the Beyond 5G/6G era.

articleTitle: Generation of Microwave Bottle Beam by a Reflective Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Bottle beam has drawn considerable research interest due to their attractive features and applications. Here, dynamic generation of bottle beams is investigated over a wide frequency band ranging from 8.5 GHz to 9.5 GHz. By studying and utilizing a varactor-diode-loaded reflective metasurface, bottle beams can be validated with different parameters and working frequencies.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Circular Polarized Type III Radio Bursts in the Inner Heliosphere
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Solar Type III radio bursts, characterized as the fast frequency drift with time, are among the most common radio emissions and are the powerful tool to diagnose the accelerated electron beams and ambient plasma medium. In this study, 42 circular polarized type III radio bursts are analyzed quantitatively using Parker Solar Probe (PSP) observations from October 2018 to May 2021. Our results reveal that the low-cutoff frequency of circular polarization signature is above 1 MHz regardless of the low-cutoff frequency of type III intensity. The maximum degree of circular polarization in most of our cases appear simultaneously or earlier than the peak total intensity. We suppose that the type III bursts with the large time lag of maximum degree of circular polarization relative to the peak total intensity might come from the harmonic emissions. This study provides a new insight into the understanding for circular polarized type III bursts.

articleTitle: Study on Electromagnetic Scattering Characteristics of Kelvin Ship Wake
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Ship wakes can effectively assist in detecting ship targets at sea due to their large geometric scale, long existence time, non-concealment and strong scattering characteristics. This paper focuses on the Kelvin wake of ship, which is more obvious in the microwave remote sensing image. The geometric model of Kelvin wake is established based on fluid dynamics. Considering the complex dielectric properties of real seawater, the dielectric constants of seawater at different frequencies are calculated by use of the double-Debye model. Considering the two-scale scattering characteristics of random rough sea surface, the spatial distribution of the scattering intensity of the wake is simulated using the semi-deterministic facet scattering model (SDFSM). The effects of ship speed, incident electromagnetic wave frequency and azimuth on the spatial distribution of the scattering intensity of the Kelvin wake at sea are fully studied. This study reveals the formation mechanism of electromagnetic imaging of ship wakes to some extent, and has important application value in the recognition and detection of naval ship targets. It can effectively assist in the establishment of wake geometric model and scattering model database, and realize machine learning with small or zero samples.

articleTitle: Design of an Integrated Rectenna on Multi-layer High-Resistivity Silicon Substrate
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a rectenna integrated on silicon, using a multilayer substrate composed of silicon and air. The rectenna is designed to harvest microwave energy at2.45 GHz. The substrate structure is composed of three layers of high-resistivity silicon (HRSi, $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}}=11.7$) where the central layer presents an air cavity obtained through etching process. The chosen feeding structure for the antenna is based on a planar microstrip feeding line while for the rectifier a planar matching network is adopted to allow the maximum power transfer. The adopted rectifier topology is a voltage doubler, consisting of a pair of Skyworks SMS7630-079LF Schottky diodes. The synthetized low-permittivity substrate is compatible with on-chip systems silicon and assure a 84 % radiation efficiency with a maximum gain of 7.76 dBi, for the patch antenna. The overall efficiency of the rectenna is 45% for a received power level of 7 dBm.

articleTitle: Weak Moving Target Detection Based on Multi-Frame Coherent Integration Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The long-time coherent integration algorithm is an effective way to improve the detection performance of weak target. However, due to the limited pulses of radar echoes in a single frame, the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) accumulated by the inter-frame integration method cannot satisfy the detection requirements. To solve this issue, a multi-frame coherent integration (including intra-frame and inter-frame integration) method is proposed. This algorithm has two stages. Firstly, the inter-frame range walk is corrected by the frequency domain correction method. After range correction, a phase compensation method is proposed to settle the phase discontinuity between adjacent frames. Secondly, the SNR of the target can be improved significantly by the multi-frame coherent integration method. The experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms the multi-frame noncoherent integration method and multi-frame moving target detection method.

articleTitle: New Signal Processing Technique Using Optical Phase Modulator and Optical Fiber Dispersion Effect
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new signal processing technique using optical phase modulator and optical fiber dispersion effect. By utilizing a silica optical fiber as a delay line in a RoF link and an optical phase modulator operating with RF wireless signals, detection and processing of RF signals are obtainable. Basic experimental results for 5G wireless band are presented.

articleTitle: Design of terahertz detector based on superconducting kinetic inductance
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: High time-frequency sampling in terahertz band has the potential to find significant discoveries, and superconducting kinetic inductance detector (KID) has the characteristics of fast response and low readout noise, which is a favorable reserve instrument for terahertz high-speed imaging detector. In this paper, we present our design of terahertz detector based on superconducting kinetic inductance effect, including six groups of comparative experiments.

articleTitle: Recent Activities of the Spectrum Management Office at the National Astronomical Observatory of Japan
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper describes the brief introduction of the radio astronomy facilities in Japan and recent activities of the Spectrum Management Office (SMO) at the National Astronomical Observatory of Japan (NAOJ). NAOJ SMO serves as the focal point for spectrum management related to radio astronomy in Japan, and works to protect radio astronomy from harmful interference by conducting sharing and compatibility studies with a variety of radio frequency applications, including Wi-Fi, vehicle-mounted radar, cellular phones, and satellite communications.

articleTitle: Construction Method of Outdoor Electromagnetic Space Based on Ubiquitous Perception Intelligent Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: A semi-automatic outdoor electromagnetic spectrum monitoring scheme is designed and implemented to study the spatial distribution characteristics of the electromagnetic field in the outdoor macro scenario. A localized statistical electromagnetic propagation model is proposed. The channel measurement system comprises an RF module, a ubiquitous sensing module, and a mechanical control platform. The RF front end uses NI-USRP 2954 as the primary RF device. Based on LabVIEW 2019, the RF control host computer is compiled for automatic power acquisition. After the fixed-point road test of the Xi’an University of Electronic Technology, the electromagnetic propagation model in ITU-R-related recommendations is used for verification, and the localization model is optimized. The measured results show that the outdoor semi-automatic electromagnetic monitoring system proposed in this paper has good robustness, the error standard deviation of the improved ITU electromagnetic propagation model is less than 7. 3dB, and the average error is less than 0.6 dB. The test system has the characteristics of automation and easy operation, which provides a new test method for the general study of electromagnetic spatial distribution in complex environments and the construction of digital electromagnetic twins.

articleTitle: Overview of Wave Propagation Effects for V2X Rooftop Antennas and Hidden Inside the Car
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The growing trend of minimizing the visual impact of antennas to preserve the aesthetics of the car leads to a degradation of the far-field radiation patterns required for V2X communication at 5.9 GHz. This contribution outlines the main electromagnetic wave phenomena causing such deterioration and presents concepts to mitigate the effects that impact the antenna’s functionality. The cumulative distribution functions of antenna gain and of signal level characterize the simulative and measured performance for rooftop antennas and those under the car roof, respectively.

articleTitle: High-Performance Radiative Near-Field Transmitter for Wireless Power Transfer to Biomedical Implants
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a high-performance transmitting antenna (Tx) for wireless power transfer (WPT) to biomedical implants. A bipolar radiating plane is configured to obtain optimal current distribution on Tx’s surface. A slotted-ring excitation structure is implemented to centrally feed radiating patch. Meanwhile, an impedance matching network (IMN) is proposed and attached to the excitation ring to match the antenna impedance to the source impedance. Moreover, an implantable receiver (Rx) is employed to verify the Tx’s performance. Verification results show that the proposed antenna can achieve a transmission efficiency of up to -17.82dB to an implantation depth of 20mm.

articleTitle: The Yebes Observatory: a bridge between the Earth and the Universe
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This contribution gives an overview of the astronomical and space-geodetic activities carried out at Yebes Observatory.

articleTitle: The importance of considering ionospheric variance for over-the-horizon radar performance modelling
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Climatological models of the ionosphere, such as the International Reference Ionosphere (IRI), are often used to assess the performance of over the horizon radar (OTHR) over the wide range of climatological conditions in which they are expected to operate. To date these models have only considered the monthly median performance. In this paper we use a new climatological model of the ionosphere which includes the monthly ionospheric variance, to investigate the impact of the variability of the ionosphere on the OTHR performance assessment models.

articleTitle: 920 MHz band rectenna with the CNT-TFT GAD
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper presents the first demonstration of rectification with the carbon nanotube thin film transistor (CNT-TFT) for wireless power transfer (WPT) in the 920 MHz band. The CNT-TFT that is a coated TFT using semiconducting single-walled carbon nanotubes has advantage of low-cost fabrication and planner integration with an antenna on a thin film. On the other, reported frequency ranges were within HF bands due to their wider channel size. For applying the CNT-TFT to GHz-order rectification, the gated anode diode (GAD) is employed and is characterized for its modeling. As the results, practical operations of 920 MHz band rectenna with the CNT-TFT GAD and the dual loop antenna can be confirmed in experimental investigations.

articleTitle: Molecular Dynamics Studies on the Effects of RF EM fields on Biological Membranes
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Radiofrequency (RF) electromagnetic (EM) fields, with frequencies above 6 GHz and into the ‘millimetre wave’ range are recently being employed for emerging telecommunication technologies, opening again the issue of investigating possible biological effects. In particular, a study on the comprehension of the basic interaction mechanisms at the cellular and molecular levels is needed. Here, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations can give the chance to evaluate the interactions between RF signals and biological matter, occurring in a nanosecond timescale at the atomistic level. Authors investigate the physical mechanisms induced on a patch of biological membrane by applying Continuous Wave (CW) signals, at 1 and 26 GHz, comparing their effects with static field ones.

articleTitle: Foster’s Reactance Theorem for a Multiport, and its Application to Q Factor Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The classical Foster’s reactance theorem relates the input impedance or admittance to the stored energy inside a lossless one-port network. Such relation has been successfully applied to the measurement of Q factor for a resonator given its one-port response. Sometimes, however, a resonator is naturally monitored at more-than-one ports. Although there are various methods for Q measurement given two-port network parameters, it remains open as for whether the Foster-based method can be extended to such scenario. In this paper, we first derive the Foster’s theorem for the multiport case, providing the relation between the stored energy and the N-port Z or Y matrix. Based on the result, we then propose a new method for Q-factor estimation. A feature of this method is that we directly use the whole Z or Y matrices to estimate Q, without reducing it to a one- or two-port network. Two simulation examples are provided to demonstrate the feasibility as well as the detailed operation of this method.

articleTitle: Linear Chirp Pulse Radar System Design and Detecting Ability Verification for Small Drone Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper discusses the detecting method of small drone by using linear chirp pulse radar system and system design. In this paper, linear frequency modulated (LFM) chirp pulse radar system for long-distance detection was used to improve distance resolution, and bistatic pulse was adopted to increase RX sensitivity. By reducing the leakage signal through IF stage switching for low cost and simplicity of the system, the noise floor was lowered and detection performance was improved through this method. In order to increase the detection ability in a multi-clutter environment, the SNR enhancement method using micro-Doppler signature (MDS) extraction and singular value decomposition (SVD) was proposed, and its validity was verified through experiments.

articleTitle: Radiated Power Prediction Model Based on Antenna Response Under the Complex Electromagnetic Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Analyzing electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) issues when there are multiple transmit and receive antennas in the environment is important and challenging. In this paper, we consider environmental information and antenna port response, modeling the perceived power of receivers in a dynamic scenario by discretizing the latitude and longitude into grid points and calculating the antenna gain at the transmitting and receiving locations, with the backdrop of a formation of aircraft and ships at sea. The proposed model can be used for interference prediction in complex electromagnetic environments.

articleTitle: Deployment of Millimeter-Wave Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface in An Indoor Scenario Based on Ray-Tracing Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: To investigate the deployment methodology of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) in an indoor scenario, a technique of incorporating the RIS into a ray-tracing simulation is studied. In this work, the effects of deploying RIS in an indoor environment are thoroughly considered by skillfully embedding the simulated radiation field pattern of RIS in the raytracing simulator. Depending on the demanded power density distribution in the target environment, the RISs can be configured by adjusting the electrical characteristics and setups such as incident angles, beamwidths, types of transmitting antennas, and so on. With this approach, the realistic impact of the 1-bit RIS unit cell are included. The capabilities/effectiveness of utilizing RISs for enhancing the communication channel can be evaluated. Specifically, the results facilitate the determination of deployment locations and parameters of RISs, thereby brining about the effective usage of RISs in actual indoor environment.

articleTitle: Signal Model and Influence Analysis of Spaceborne SAR Images in the Presence of Mutual Terrain-Scattered Interference
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Since the development of satellite technology and limited spectrum resources, more and more spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems share the same frequency band. For this reason, a new form of radio frequency interference (RFI), i.e., mutual terrain scattering interference (MTSI), will be occurred between different spaceborne SARs in the case of overlapping time, space, and frequency, seriously degrading the imaging quality. This paper investigates the signal model and impact of spaceborne SAR images in the presence of MTSI. We first established a geometric model of the interference propagation path, from which the mechanism of interference is analyzed, and derive the signal model and energy of echoes. Then, simulated experiments using RADARSAT images are provided to illustrate the relationship between various radar parameters and resulting interference artifacts, which could be beneficial for interference identification and mitigation.

articleTitle: Measurements and Analysis of Angular Channel Characteristics in Substation Scenarios for Power IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: To support the implementation of wireless communication technologies in power Internet of Things (PIoT), channel measurements and characterization for typical electrical scenarios should be investigated. In this work, we present a phased array antenna-based channel sounder and propose a multipath components (MPCs) extraction algorithm for directional channel measurements. The field tests are conducted in a 110 kV GIS room and a semi-indoor 110 kV substation to measure the angular channel characteristics, including the power angle delay profile and the angle spread of departure and arrival. These results can contribute to the planning and optimization of PIoT wireless communication system.

articleTitle: Current Trends and Approaches to improve Self-Interference Cancellation at the RF Domain across a Wide Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: To double spectrum efficiency, a well-known approach uses simultaneous transmit and receiver (STAR) radios. The goal is to suppress the coupling from the transmitter to the receiver, using the knowledge of the transmitted signal. Successful implementation of STAR requires self-interference cancellation of at least 100 dB across the entire band. Notably, sufficient isolation between the Tx/Rx signal must be achieved to avoid saturation in the LNA and other components in the Rx chain. In the past, STAR realizations were narrowband. This paper presents current trends and approaches to achieve improved Tx-Rx isolation across a wideband channel of 1 GHz, as required by 6G and future applications. Measurements show that a combined 2-stage isolation of > 65 dB can be achieved.

articleTitle: Design considerations of navigation satellite constellation for low Earth orbit
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this study we provide an overview of feasibility assessment of Low Earth Orbit Position, Timing and Navigation (LEO-PNT) satellite system. We discuss several aspects of such a design, such as signal design, accuracy assessment, satellite constellation design, satellite payload design and satellite platform design. We conclude, that such a system is feasible and provide general parameters for implementation.

articleTitle: Polar Ionospheric TEC Enhancement Observation Using GNSS-R
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper presents recent processing results of ionospheric TEC enhancement obtained over the Arctic and Antarctic based on GNSS reflectometry (GNSS-R) measurements. The polar ionosphere is home for many interesting and dynamic processes. Yet, ionospheric observations at polar regions are sparse due to challenges in deploying instruments in the harsh environments. GNSS-R offers a promising new means to fill the data gap at high latitudes by utilizing coherently reflected signal over ice and received by LEO satellite equipped with side- or downward looking antennas. This paper presents real grazing angle GNSS-R data collected by Spire Global CubeSats to retrieve ionospheric TEC over the Arctic and Antarctic. This paper show examples of GNSS-R observations of ionospheric TEC enhancement over the Arctic and Antarctica.

articleTitle: Novel Dual-polarized MIMO Antennas in 60-GHz AiP Module for Full Polarimetric Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper presents a 60-GHz dual polarized MIMO antenna for full polarimetric radar antenna-in-packaging (AiP) module. The proposed MIMO antenna consists of two orthogonally arranged dual-polarized cavity-backed co-located aperture antennas. The simulated results show that the proposed antenna has excellent performances, such as wideband impedance bandwidth covers the operational frequency band, the promising radiation efficiency, a stable and wide radiation pattern, and most importantly the superior port and polarization isolation. This innovative antenna design combines a cavity-backed aperture with spatial and polarization diversity. The idea of gathering the full polarimetric matrix can be achieved using Time Division Duplexing (TDD) to switch between Tx1 and Tx2 antenna for further studies. The proposed dual-polarized antenna is a suitable candidate of 60-GHz AiP module for full polarimetric radar applications.

articleTitle: A model local interpretation routine for deep learning based radio galaxy classification
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Radio galaxy morphological classification is one of the critical steps when producing source catalogues for large-scale radio continuum surveys. While many recent studies attempted to classify source radio morphology from survey image data using deep learning algorithms (i.e., Convolutional Neural Networks), they concentrated on model robustness most time. It is unclear whether a model similarly makes predictions as radio astronomers did. In this work, we used Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanation (LIME), an state-of-the-art eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) technique to explain model prediction behaviour and thus examine the hypothesis in a proof-of-concept manner. In what follows, we describe how LIME generally works and early results about how it helped explain predictions of a radio galaxy classification model using this technique.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>Hongming Tang and Shiyu Yue have equally contributed to this work.

articleTitle: Analytical Channel Model for On-Body Antenna at 60 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this study, we proposed an analytical channel model for the assessment of on-body wireless system performances at millimeter-wave frequencies. The combined effects of direct on-body link and multipath fading components with dynamic characteristics of human walking motion was modeled by Monte Carlo simulation. The statistical distribution of signals shows that the Rician channel property at 60 GHz is well modeled using the proposed method. With the variations in Rice factor, the cross-polarized antenna performs well for accounting for the dynamic characteristics of mmWave on-body channels compared to linearly polarization antennas.

articleTitle: Examining the Feasibility of Flexible Coaxial-Probe-based Dielectric Sensing of Tissue Properties
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The measurement of dielectric properties of biological tissues is vital for numerous applications, including as the foundation for microwave (MW) diagnostic and therapeutic technologies. A rigid open-ended coaxial probe is typically used for dielectric measurements across the MW range. However, rigid tools cannot easily reach all tissues, limiting the potential in vivo measurements that can be achieved. Therefore, this work presents a numerical study of a flexible coaxial probe for in vivo tissue measurements.

articleTitle: A 300 GHz Resonant Cavity Antenna using a Frequency Selective Surface on a Quartz Substrate
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper presents a resonant cavity antenna based on a patch antenna and a frequency selective surface operating at 300 GHz. A microstrip patch antenna on a quartz substrate is fabricated using the integrated passive device technology. To further enhance the antenna gain, a metamaterial layer is introduced on the backside of the substrate as a frequency selective surface and a resonator is thus formed. Gain enhancement due to the resonator is about 6 dB.

articleTitle: Three-mirror anastigmatic five-meter aperture telescope and camera optics for CMB-S4
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The next-generation ground-based cosmic microwave background (CMB) experiment, CMB-S4 will map the cosmic microwave background in degree and arcminute angular scales. Inflationary science benefits from the use of a large-aperture, arcminute resolution delensing survey, able to observe a large field of view of 9 degrees at wavelengths as short as $\lambda = 1 .1$ mm. In this work we review the optical design of the three-mirror anastigmatic large-aperture CMB-S4 telescope and its array of optics tubes. This optical system is capable mapping the CMB with unprecedented levels of sensitivity.

articleTitle: Machine Learning with Wearable RFID Grid for Monitoring Fetal Movements
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Fetal movements are crucial signs of the fetus’ well-being and are clinically monitored with self-reports or wearable detectors. However, wired detectors worsen mothers’ labour, and wireless ones are still not adopted due to their higher cost. Radiofrequency identification (RFID) can be exploited to develop low-cost solutions for detecting fetal movements based on tag response variations. In this contribution, a wearable RFID grid for fetal monitoring is manufactured and tested. Even though the backscattered EM wave unpredictably changes when tags are displaced by a probe emulating a foot of a 20-week-old fetus, a decision tree for classification detected motionless and moving tags with accuracy $\gt 91$% in the preliminary test.

articleTitle: Identification of optimal transcutaneous electrical stimulation waveforms for pain relief
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In recent years, chronic pain relief by inducing endogenous opioids has attracted attention. One mechanism for inducing endogenous opioids is electrical stimulation of the C nerve near the fascia. However, the feasibility of non-invasive selective stimulation by transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) has yet to be studied. In this study, we proposed a novel TENS waveform identification method for selective C nerve stimulation. The method consists of a surrogate model learned from a TENS multi-tissue conduction model implemented with a finite element, and an optimization process for fast and extensive exploration of different stimulation waveforms, which is enabled by the surrogate model. The results showed that transcutaneous pulse stimulation with a carrier frequency of 100 Hz showed better selectivity of the C nerve than near-myofascial pulse stimulation in comparison with other frequencies investigated. At this frequency, the current density near the nerve contains a damper component added to the original transcutaneous waveform for dealing with the capacitance effect of the biological tissue. By leveraging this active damper effect using a suitable pre-pulse at the rising edge of the transcutaneous pulse, it was possible to improve the selectivity of the C fiber as a step toward realizing TENS for chronic pain relief.

articleTitle: Device Placement Problem Analysis in General-Purpose Microwave Photonic Processors (GPMWPPs) Implemented using Barium Titanate Based Electro-optically Tunable Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: GPMWPP is a recent and innovative field for implementing parallel processing in photonic integrated circuits. Light distribution in these circuits is controlled via tunable MZIs using the thermo-optic effect which increases the dependencies on the high-performance blocks due to slower response time and smaller operational bandwidths. To address this limitation, GPMWPPs can be implemented using electro-optic effect offered by BTO devices. However, due to inherent anisotropy associated with BTO correct placement of devices, achieving identical performance for devices in various orientations becomes a challenge. In this work we propose a solution addressing the device placement problem in GPMWPP circuits.

articleTitle: Modeling Atmosphere-Ionosphere Coupling on Gravity Waves during 2019 Typhoon 15 and 19 using FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Atmospheric Gravity Waves (AGWs) are important phenomena that propagate heat to wider areas in the atmosphere through heat convection. It is especially occurred during typhoons, propagating radially from the typhoon’s eye. UEC’s VLF network has two parallel paths from the VLF transmitter NPM in Hawaii to receiving stations Moshiri (MSR) and Yamaguchi (YMG) in Japan to monitor the ionospheric perturbation due to powerful typhoons. These paths are used to observe the propagation of the gravity waves during Typhoons 15 and 19 in 2019 which occurred in the Pacific Ocean. The spectrum intensity of VLF signals on NPM-YMG and NPM-MSR showed that there is the possibility of AGWs occurrence on September $4 ^{th}$ and $5 ^{th}$ during Typhoon 15 and October $7 ^{th}$ and $8 ^{th}$ during Typhoon 19. The spatial dependence of ionospheric perturbation is modeled using a 2D Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD). The perturbation height variations on NPM-YMG and NPM-MSR from the simulation are then compared to the fluctuation of the observation VLF signal during Typhoons. The ionospheric perturbation variation over time shows a similar fluctuation pattern on September $4 ^{th}$ and $5 ^{th}$ during Typhoon 15 in NPM-YMG and NPM-MSR with a delay of 2.5 hours and 2 hours respectively. It fluctuated in the ionospheric height between 88 km to 83 km over 2 hours period. This fluctuation indicates the amplitude of the gravity wave propagation. It is then calculated that the gravity waves on Typhoon 15 have a phase velocity of 94.2 m/s and 117.8 m/s on September $4 ^{th}$ and $5 ^{th}$ respectively.

articleTitle: Ideas for Radar Data Denoising and Fusion Based on Image Processing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: We propose novel denoising and fusion schemes for radar data of distributed targets. To utilize established image processing techniques, we consider the denoising and fusion as image reconstruction in the Cartesian coordinates from the noisy data in the polar coordinates. We reconstruct the target image as the solution to a minimization problem with a regularization term. Denoising simulation in an attenuation correction scenario demonstrates the proposed scheme with the total variation regularization greatly reduces the noise.

articleTitle: On the Use of Planar Skin Models in High Frequency Dosimetry Assessment
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The paper is on the use of a surface integral equation (SIE) based formulation and the conventional method of moments (MoM) in high frequency dosimetry. The investigation is carried out, whether the reduced planar models, could latter be utilized in the assessment of spatial averaging of absorbed power density (APD) at frequencies of 10 and 30 GHz. Some numerical results illustrating the distribution of the surface electric field and the convergence of several electric field measures, including maximum and average values, are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network for Radar-based Respiration Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: A continuous wave (CW) radar system that is designed to detect respiration and heart rate of a human, is presented. The radar operates at 5.8 GHz and has two outputs, the in-phase (I) and quadrature (Q) signals. The respiration and heartbeat frequencies can be extracted by processing these outputs using traditional methods, such as Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and simple peak searches. Emphasis is given to the developed artificial neural network (ANN) used to determine the respiration frequency of the waveform. The motivation is that ANNs are faster than FFT-based approaches. The proposed method consists of training, validating and testing the ANN model with digitally constructed waves emulating respiration waveforms. Real world scenario measurement data from the CW radar system are then fed to the ANN model and the respiration frequency is obtained consistently. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach is on average 91.84% accurate and effective.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Classification and Prediction of Electromagnetic Absorption in Electrical Reverberation Chambers
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: A method is proposed to quickly classify devices with regard to their susceptibility to absorb power from an ambient electromagnetic field with the help of an electrical reverberation chamber. Different absorption classes are implemented via a set of labeled training devices. Frequency depending S-parameters are considered as data. The machine learning environment consists of an auto-encoder to reduce the dimension of the input data and several machine learning approaches for classification.

articleTitle: Armed Microstrip Patch: New Configuration with Promising Feature of High 3D Cross-Polar Discrimination
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This work explores a novel approach of controlling cross-polar (XP) radiations of a microstrip patch without tampering its ground plane or introducing any additional engineering. It proposes a new possibility where the patch geometry could be improvised without involving any expensive design or fabrication procedures. This, to the best of our knowledge, is the first of its kind which promises at least 10dB XP reduction over its diagonal plane without any rigorous feeding or structural engineering. The proposed geometry has also been experimentally tested and extended to realize improved array revealing equal amount of XP reduction over 3D radiation planes.

articleTitle: Radar signal deinterleaving method exploiting correlation of multi-parameter time series
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Signal deinterleaving is a critical technique in the process of radar electronic reconnaissance. However, the performance of the traditional signal deinterleaving algorithm is degraded dramatically when faced with high pulse loss ratios and noise pulse interference. To deal with this deficiency, a radar signal deinterleaving method exploiting the correlation of multi-parameter time series is proposed. TOA, RF, and PW are used to construct a pulse feature representation. The bidirectional recurrent neural network is used to explore the long-term temporal patterns in the pulse stream and extract the characteristics of the pulse time series context via supervised learning. Simulated experimental results showed that the proposed method could obtain robust performance under non-ideal conditions, which can achieve an accuracy of over 90% even if the pulse loss ratio reached 70%.

articleTitle: Radar Cross Section Measurements on Wind Turbines in VHF Band
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This work is using a new method allowing to identify reflecting objects in the surrounding area of Doppler VHF Omnidirectional Radio-range (DVOR) transmitters. It is based on a bi-static, partially cooperative Radar application. Here, this method is applied – using received signal power measurements – to derive a quantitative value of an equivalent radar cross section (RCS) of wind turbines. The analysis is focussed on wind turbines in a distance of 5 to 12 km around a DVOR transmitter in Hehlingen, Germany.

articleTitle: Design of Spatially-Dispersive Beam-Steering Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this work, we explore the design and applications of spatially-dispersive beam-steering metasurfaces. Such innovative devices consist of cascaded Huygens meta-atoms optimized to exhibit an engineered profile of their transmission phase vs. the incidence angle of the impinging wave. Differently from conventional beam-steering metasurfaces, the proposed devices exhibit a refraction effect that is strongly angle-dependent and may find application in several scenarios of future wireless systems.

articleTitle: Reduce Size, High Power mmWave Phased-Array Antenna System with Integrated Compound Semiconductor Power Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new design of a high-power phased-array antenna system for low-earth orbit (LEO) satellite communication and 5G communications using compound semiconductor power amplifiers such as Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) and Gallium Nitride (GaN) that provides 78 dBm EIRP (Effective Isotropic Radiated Power) and improved power efficiency. The phased-array design offers several benefits such as precise and efficient communication, improved link budget, and high pointing accuracy for LEO satellite communication and high gain and low side lobes for 5G. This proposed design is an ideal solution for both LEO satellite communication and 5G applications where high performance and compactness is required.

articleTitle: Hawaii Fast Radio Burst Outrigger Station
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: A hybrid array of radio telescope antennas is planned for deployment on the Big Island of Hawaii to serve as an outrigger station to the CHIME FRB telescope located in British Columbia. The array will consist of ten 6-meter dishes and twelve log periodic antennas designed to operate in the 400 to 800 MHz band. This paper summarizes the early stages of preparation and tests conducted to date.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis of Si-Photonics-Based In-Vehicle Optical Network (SiPhON)
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Our research project has been developing Si-photonics-based in-vehicle optical network (SiPhON) for low latency, high capacity, and high reliability in-vehicle network. In this paper, we present theoretical analyses of the reliability on SiPhON and compare the reliability with IEEE P802.3cz-based in-vehicle optical networks. Our results show that SiPhON achieves higher reliability with temperature-controlled DFB-LDs.

articleTitle: Evaluation on Correlation between M-curve and Overreach Duct Propagation from Korea to Japen in V-Low Band
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
