articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Polarization Reconfigurable Circularly Polarized Antenna with Wide Axial Ratio bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper presents a reconfigurable right-handed/left-handed circularly polarized (RHCP/LHCP) antenna with wide axial ratio bandwidth for 5G millimeter-wave applications. Each of the CP elements comprises two parasitic trapezoid patches and three suspended metallic vias, and is excited through an aperture coupling technique with the help of a cross-slot geometry. Two such elements are diagonally connected with the feedline by using p-i-n diodes, which help in achieving the switching between the RHCP and LHCP behaviors. The designed antenna produces wide 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) under both cases, viz. 21.5- 27.55 GHz during LHCP and 23.5- 28.70 GHz during RHCP condition. A good gain of 6.5 dBic over the operating bandwidth has also been achieved for both cases in the broadside direction. The concept is well investigated with the help of parametric variations, surface current distributions, and other critical antenna parameters.

articleTitle: Evaluation of biological effects by exposure to 60 GHz millimeter wave in reconstructed human tissue model
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this study, biological effects by exposure to 60 GHz millimeter wave for 6 minutes was investigated using reconstructed human 3-dimensional tissue models. Especially, this study is related to in vivo rabbit cornea studies conducted by Kojima et al. and exposure environment was adjusted to surface of cornea in the rabbit studies. Threshold of toxicity and altar of gene expression was discussed.

articleTitle: Type III Radio Bursts from Solar Eruptions and their Connection to GLE and SGRE Events
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: We report on the close similarity of coronal mass ejection (CME) properties in ground level enhancement (GLE) in solar energetic particle (SEP) events and sustained gammaray emission (SGRE) from the Sun as indicated by low frequency type III radio bursts observed in the interplanetary medium. The complex type III bursts have an average 1 MHz duration of 36 and 34 min in the SGRE and GLE events, respectively. Similarly, the CMEs underlying SGRE and GLE have average space speeds of 1866 and 2084 km/s, respectively. These are larger than the corresponding values (32 min, 1407 km/s) for a control sample of type III bursts associated with frontside halo CMEs with sky-plane speed >800 km/s. These results are consistent with the idea that energetic CME-drive shocks accelerate particles to very high energies that are responsible for GLE and SGRE events.

articleTitle: A study on shadowing caused by a metallic object placed near LCX antenna of 920MHz-band RFID system
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper describes the shadowing effect caused by a metallic object which is placed close to 920MHz-band RFID reader/writer antenna. Two kinds of antennas, a conventional patch antenna and a leaky coaxial cable (LCX) antenna, are examined by electro-magnetic (EM) simulation. It shows that the LCX antenna has smaller shadowed area than the conventional patch antenna.

articleTitle: A Broadband Ka-Band Reconfigurable Reflectarray Utilizing Dumbbell-Shaped Unit Cells
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: A 1-bit reconfigurable reflectarray (RRA) designed with the dumbbell-shaped unit cells is proposed. The cell structure is implemented using four metal PCB consisting of the radiation, ground, RF choke, and DC bias layers. The RRA is designed for the 5G application operating at n257 frequency band. The simulation shows cells bandwidth of 19% covering 24.9 GHz to 30.1 GHz, which meets the designate bandwidth requirements. Specifically, the peak simulated gain of the 1600-cell RRA is 29.4 dB while the achievable beam scanning range is ±60°.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Exposure from Wireless Devices as Function of Distance
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: A measurement study has been conducted to understand the relationship between user exposure and distance of the wireless device to the body. This topic is pressing given the recent proposal of the European Committee for Electrotechnical Standardization (CENELEC) to perform Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) testing at 0 mm distance to the body for body-worn test conditions. Based on the two main interaction mechanisms of the coupling of the incident fields with tissue simulating media [1, 2], a monotonic increase of the induced fields with reduced distance is expected. However, early research has already shown that proximity of the user may detune the transmitter structure. This may result in a higher SAR at distances greater than 0 mm to the body. This topic deserves a thorough and comprehensive study so that a standardized testing procedure can be proposed that is both conservative and easy to implement with minimal impact on test time. The results of this study are regularly presented to relevant standards bodies.

articleTitle: Comparison between RO and Digisonde ionospheric peak characteristics over low-latitudes
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The objective of this study is to perform a comparison between ionospheric characteristics (foF2, hmF2) as measured from the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) radio occultation (RO) FORMOSAT7/COSMIC2 (F7/C2) constellation mission along with collocated (in space and time) manually scaled data from Digisondes at Fortaleza, Cachoeira Paulista and Santa Maria. This preliminary comparison demonstrates that there is no clear systematic latitude dependent discrepancy between the two techniques, as established by past studies based on FORMOSAT3/COSMIC (F3/C) measurements. However there is evidence to suggest that over each station this discrepancy varies in accordance to solar activity in terms of hmF2.

articleTitle: Using Babinet’s principle in plasmonics for dielectric sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Plasmonic structures that exhibit localized surface plasmon (LSP) resonances have been exploited in multiple applications including sensing, medicine, and chemistry. LSPs resonances appearing in, for instance, periodic/aperiodic rods or spheres have been recently used for sensing due to the fact that such resonances are sensitive to local external variations such as changes in the refractive index of a dielectric placed on top of them. In this communication, we make use of complementary plasmonic structures (exploiting the Babinet’s principle) consisting of metal-dielectric cylindrical components to study their performance as dielectric film sensors. An in-depth comparison of the complementary structures with the original plasmonic configurations is carried out demonstrating the advantages/disadvantages of each design.

articleTitle: BLT-Based Field Coupling to Microstrip Network Model Enabling Radiated Immunity Assessment for PCB Wiring Design
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper proposed a statistical approach for assessing the radiated immunity of microstrip networks. For this purpose, electromagnetic field coupling to PCB is formulated by exploring the Baum-Liu-Tesche (BLT) equation, where special attention is focused on the field multi-reflections in dielectric substrate layer. Owing to the computational efficiency of deterministic model, a Monte-Carlo simulation is proposed to predict the statistical distributions and upper bound of terminal voltage across microstrip networks. The approach is then applied to compare the radiated immunity of canonical wiring layout design, which offers guidelines for improving microstrip designs.

articleTitle: An Antenna Far-field Prediction Method Based on Shooting and Bouncing Ray Method
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The shooting and bouncing ray (SBR) method is a general and efficient estimation method for calculating the radar scattering cross-section of complex targets of electric universities. In this paper, the SBR method is used to analyze the distortion of the far-field directional map of the electric large platform antenna, and the far-field magnitude at each target observation angle is obtained by invoking the ray-tracking module’s ray magnitude tracking and ray phase tracking for calculation, then the antenna far-field is quickly calculated by collecting the field strength contribution of the rays at each target observation angle. This method overcomes the problem that needs to consume huge memory and computation time, and avoids the calculation frequency changes due to the algorithm and requires recalculation. The method was compared with a Cassegrain antenna excited by an 18 GHz horn antenna, and it was concluded that SBR greatly improved the computational efficiency of the antenna far field.

articleTitle: Location of Ionospheric Irregularities in Extended GNSS-RO Measurements Using Back Propagation Method
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Besides providing electron density profiles (EDP), GNSS Radio Occultation (GNSS-RO) measurements allow monitoring the frequency and the areas where ionospheric scintillations occur. In this work, RO measurements composing an experimental data set are processed with the back propagation (BP) method to estimate the location of sporadic E-clouds and equatorial plasma bubbles (EPB). The data set includes non-conventional measurements tracked up to 600 km (generally around 80 km), covering F-region heights, shortly before MetOp-A was decommissioned. Results indicate the combination of extended occultations and the BP method is promising for monitoring the occurrence and characterizing ionospheric irregularities in the F-region and the E-region.

articleTitle: Interference Type Recognition in Spaceborne SARs Image Based on Deep CNN Model
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Interference has an adverse impact on spaceborne SAR image interpretation, and mainly originates from terrestrial radio emitters. In recent years, a new type of mutual terrain scattered interference (MTSI) originating from other satellites also draw great attention, whose signal characteristics and resulting image artifacts are totally different from terrestrial interference. Determining the presence and type of interference in SAR images is an indispensable step before interference mitigation. In this paper, a novel interference recognition model using a deep convolutional neural network combined with attention mechanism is proposed. Combined with the attention mechanism, Resnet focuses on the changes in local interference regions and extracts the interference features in the image to distinguish interference. The distinction of MTSI and different kinds of terrestrial interference can be used as pre-processing before interference suppression. The experiments show that the proposed method outperforms other models on real measured Sentinel-1A data.

articleTitle: Bi-directional Dual Band Antenna Development for Wi-Fi Applications in Street Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: A bi-directional antenna development for Wi-Fi 2.4/5 GHz band operations were presented in this paper. The proposed antenna consists of two slot-coupled microstrip antenna arrays with ± 45° dual slant polarization which are excited by stripline-fed through slot aperture in the metal ground planes on the upper and lower surface of the feeding substrate, and then the field is coupled to the radiator on both side antenna substrates with air gap to achieve bidirectional radiation pattern properties for Wi-Fi dual band multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) applications. A sandwich dielectric substrate is composed of two layers RO4000 series laminates and one-layer prepreg bonding materials and used as a stripline-to-microstrip line feeding network circuit board. This feeding configuration is located between slot aperture ground plane to serve as the entire aperture coupling structure use, and it’s also easy to integrate with RF coaxial cable for such a transmission line transition design. Simulation results verify that such a stripline-fed slot-coupled microstrip antenna construct can provide highly symmetrical bi-directional radiation pattern characteristics, is therefore suitable as potential candidates for bi-directional coverage of Wi-Fi applications in street scenarios.

articleTitle: A Frequency Selective Surface based Polarization-Independent Band Notched Electromagnetic (EM) Wave Absorber
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This work presents an EM wave absorber with a band notch between the absorption band. The proposed work consists of two vertically arranged FSS-based resonators over a common metal on the bottom side. The SMD resistor loaded top FSS pattern offers wide absorption bandwidth, and the bottom FSS pattern provides the band notch between the absorption band. The simulation results show that the proposed structure offers more than 90% absorption in 5.8-12.9 GHz and 14.48-20.8 GHz frequency bands with a reflection notch at 13.5 GHz with a 3dB bandwidth of 500 MHz. The designed structure is also polarization-independent due to the four-fold symmetry inside the resonator. Analysis of the proposed structure's angular stability shows that the presented design is angularly stable up to 50° and 40° for TE and TM polarization, respectively. The proposed structure is compact in nature with the unit cell dimension of $0.19 \lambda_{L} \times 0.19 \lambda_{L} \times 0.12 \lambda_{L}$, where $\lambda_{L}$ is the wavelength's lowest frequency. Due to presence of the notch band along with absorption, this structure can be used for RCS reduction application of antenna where the notch band can be used as reflector of the antenna.

articleTitle: Large Scale Traveling Ionospheric Disturbances during geomagnetic storms in the Australian region
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Large-scale travelling ionospheric disturbances (LSTIDs) are detected using the critical frequency of the $F_{2}$ layer $( f_{o}F_{2})$ of the ionosphere. The HF interferometry (HF-Int) technique is applied to the network of ionosondes in the Australian region to detect and estimate propagation parameters. Here we present traveling ionospheric disturbances (TIDs) characteristics (period, velocity, and intensity) associated with selected geomagnetic storms. The TID response during geomagnetic storms varies significantly owing to the differing storm evolution patterns. Results show the morphology of parameters detected continually changes with time corresponding to highly dynamic response effects on the ionosphere. TIDs detected had a wide range of velocity magnitudes (mean ± standard deviation) such as $687 \pm 16\mathrm{m} /\mathrm{s}$ during onset phase, $516 \pm 125\mathrm{m} /\mathrm{s}$ during main phase and $569 \pm 91\mathrm{m} /\mathrm{s}$ during the recovery phase of the storm presented here. Propagation directions are predominantly equatorward with east and west deviations owing to higher latitude source generations associated with storm induced intensifications. The HF-Int system uses spectral techniques to estimate the dominant period and outputs the spectral energy contribution (SEC) which is a measure of the contribution of the TID to the total variability of the time series. TID activity levels are based on SEC criteria mostly indicated moderate and weak events with a range of periods 60-140 min.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Polarized Anomalous Electromagnetic Diffraction via the Ground Surface PlasmaWave Associated with Earthquakes
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Anomalous diffractions of radiowaves that are polarized perpendicular to the surface of the landform are observed before earthquakes. The mechanism of the diffraction has been studied by numerical analysis using the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method by implementing the three-dimensional (3D) digital elevation model (DEM) of the actual landform of mountain peaks and coastlines, which reasonably explains the observed phenomena.

articleTitle: A statistical analysis of GNSS-derived 2014 mid-latitude TEC climate at Matera, Italy
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Total Electron Content (TEC) is a result of ionospheric, geomagnetic, and space weather conditions and processes, rather than being their descriptor. The mid-latitude TEC climate over a year is examined in relation to geomagnetic disturbances to provide a quantitative analysis of TEC climate in all possible TEC dynamics event classes, while identifying their proportionate frequency of occurrence. Research outcomes are to assist the mitigation of ionospheric conditions and effects on technology systems, such as Global Satellite Navigation System (GNSS).

articleTitle: Pan-Arctic GNSS INfrastructure for Atmospheric science: state of the art of the PAGINA project
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The Italian Arctic program has recently approved the PAGINA (Pan-Arctic GNSS INfrastructure for Atmospheric Science) project. PAGINA aims to fill the existing gap of observing GNSS systems and related ICT platforms over the Arctic region by gathering the GNSS information acquired at Svalbard, Finland, Greenland, and Canada. The unprecedented effort represents the unique infrastructure capable of monitoring and investigating the northern polar atmosphere utilizing high-rate GNSS data. The novelty stands in the integration of different data sources managed by INGV (Svalbard and Greenland), UNB (Canada) and FMI (Finland), creating a bi-continental infrastructure.

articleTitle: Research on Voltage Fluctuation Calibration Method Based on Hilbert Transformation
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper describes a research on voltage fluctuation calibration in the field of power quality measurement. By comparing the existing detection methods and analyzing the mathematical model, a calibration method of voltage fluctuation signal based on Hilbert Transformation is proposed and a calibration system is also established. The experiments indicates that the voltage fluctuation can be calibrated by the system accurately which is covering frequency range 0.008 Hz to 40 Hz, and fluctuation range of 0.1% to 30%.

articleTitle: Global Ionospheric Electron Density from GNSS-POD Limb Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: GNSS-LEO radio links from Precise Orbital Determination (POD) and Radio Occultation (RO) antennas have been used increasingly in studying and monitoring the global ionospheric electron density $(N_{e})$. In this study we developed an optimal estimation (OE) method to retrieve Ne profiles from the slant total electron content $(hTEC)$ measurements acquired by the GNSS-POD links at negative elevation angles. The hmF2 and NmF2 from the OE retrieval are validated against ground-based ionosondes and radar observations, showing generally good agreements in NmF2 from all sites. Nighttime hmF2 measurements tend to agree better than the daytime when the ionosonde heights tend to be slightly lower. The OE algorithm has been applied to all GNSS-POD data acquired from the COSMIC-1 (2006-2019), COSMIC-2 (2019-present), and Spire (2019-present) constellations, showing a consistent ionospheric $N_{e}$ morphology. A detailed analysis of the frequency-wavenumber spectra is made for the $N_{e}$ variability at different heights. In the lower ionosphere (~150 km) we found significant spectral power in DE1, DW6, DW4, SW5, and SE4 wave components, in addition to well-known DW1, SW2 and DE3 waves. In the upper ionosphere (~450 km), additional wave components are still present, including DE4, DW4, DW6, SE4 and SW4. The co-exist of eastward and westward propagating WN4 components implies the presence of a stationary planetary wave4 (sPW4), as suggested by other earlier studies.

articleTitle: Multidimensional Optical Diffraction using Tensor Train Decompositions
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Multidimensional optical simulations could require impractical computer storage/time. Multidimensional array (Tensor) based representations of multivariable functions could significantly overcome these difficulties. We present a novel tensor-based formulation, and computationally efficient simulation results, of diffraction by a planar aperture of a three-dimensional optical distribution using a Tensor Train Decomposition.

articleTitle: Reconfigurability of Wired Antennas Enabled by Conformal Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The possibilities enabled by conformal cylindrical metasurfaces in modifying the characteristics of wired antennas are discussed. In particular, we show that both the electrical and radiative properties can be tuned by acting only on the electromagnetic response of the augmented wrapping surface. Two relevant examples are presented. First, the design of a dipole antenna made frequency reconfigurable thanks to the control of the surface impedance values of the cylindrical coating is presented. Then, the case of a Huygens metasurface exploited for introducing beamforming functionalities to a single dipole is illustrated.

articleTitle: Efficient Deconvolution of a Heterogeneous Array Observation Using a Direction-Dependent Point Spread Function
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: For large aperture arrays like LOFAR and SKA-LOW, the point spread function (PSF) varies significantly across the wide field-of-view (FoV) of these instruments. This turns deconvolution into a computationally demanding and often labour intensive task when using standard algorithms assuming that the PSF is constant over the FoV. In this contribution, we describe an implementation of deconvolution using a direction-dependent (DD) PSF. We demonstrate the advantage of using a DD PSF on an extreme case of a LOFAR observation done with stations of two different sizes. The use of a DD PSF made convergence of deconvolution more robust thereby requiring fewer major cycles and less manual tuning to obtain a good deconvolved image.

articleTitle: GPS-based verticality approximation of an experimental fully-airborne VLF antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Verticality, a parameter calculated as a difference between the positions of the upper and lower ends of a long, aerostat- or aircraft-supported antenna, divided by the antenna’s length, is an important parameter describing the spatial form of the very low frequency (VLF) antenna, crucial for the assessment of its operation efficiency. In this paper, a fully-airborne (not anchored) VLF test antenna is analyzed in the terms of its verticality during the ascending phase of its flight, including flight in the proximity of the stratospheric jet stream. The unsynchronized GPS data from the antenna’s proximities are used to determine the verticality with defined accuracy. The limits of this method are shown, with the possible ameliorations in order to refine the data collection and expand the range of their usefulness towards the overall antenna design.

articleTitle: Influence of the Supporting Material on the Conical Monopole Sensor Calibration Setup
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this paper the influence of the supporting material on the electric response of the conical-monopole-based sensor calibration setup is analyzed and presented. The analysis is supported by numerical simulations and measurements of the impedance response. The electric field in the region of influence is also calculated. Two different use cases for the base support of the conical monopole are presented as a comparative analysis.

articleTitle: 3D Topology of the Transient Bifurcation on the Verge of Substorm Onset
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper reports a transient bifurcation in a 3D terrestrial magnetospheric topology on the verge of the substorm onset in a 3D global MHD simulation. The 2D manifolds of the separatrices are determined using the Geodesic Level Set method. The separatrices are determined starting from the magnetic nulls or critical points near Earth’s north and south poles and magnetotail. We visualize the Earth magnetospheric topologies at different times near the substorm onset and identify a particular pair of saddle-connected separatrices that include two separator lines. They are both bifurcated toward north and south, thus, and allows the southward IMF to connect to the Earth magnetic field. This special topology appears on the verge of the substorm onset.

articleTitle: 28GHz-Band Antenna-Coupled Electrode Electro-Optic Modulator for Receiving Two Orthogonal Polarization Components Simultaneously
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: We have been studying an antenna-coupled electrode electro-optic (EO) modulator based on an antenna-coupled-electrode on LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-crystal. EO modulators are applicable as a passive wireless-optical signal converter with an integration of planar antenna and are expected to be a key device for the realization of “Massive Machine Type Communications” in Fifth-generation (5G) mobile communication systems. An antenna-coupled electrode EO modulator is also applicable for an EO senser for quasi-millimeter and millimeter wave. In this paper, we report on a new antenna-coupled electrode EO modulator that can receive two orthogonal polarization components simultaneously. The ability to simultaneously receive two orthogonal polarization components is effective for expanding communication capability. The experimental results of good polarization separation, directivity and data transfers are reported.

articleTitle: Phased Array of Dielectric Tapered Antenna at 300 GHz band
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: We show the basic characteristics of a phased array of dielectric tapered antenna operating at 300-GHz band based on a simulation. We examined antenna gain, radiation pattern, and beam steering characteristics. In the 4-element linear array configuration, we achieved the maximum antenna gain of 17.4 dBi and the beam steering range of ± 31 °.

articleTitle: Leakage losses of a capacitive power transfer parallel four plate coupler
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In spite of significant research, capacitive power transfer is not able yet to match the same power densities as inductive power transfer. One reason is the lack of models that take energy transfer through solid media into account. This paper bridges the gap by introducing the capacitive coupling-induced leakage resistance.The leakage resistance is simulated using an analytical approach and with finite element simulations coupled to a power electronics simulation. This approach reveals that the losses in media have a significant impact on the efficiency: In an exemplary case, polycarbonate dissipates 30% of the transferred power.

articleTitle: Conditions (technically and regularly) for finding a new access to SST measurements in the microwave area: band sharing is the way
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Based on the studies performed in International Telecommunication Union sector Radiocommunication (ITU-R) under agenda item 1.2 (A.I 1.2) of the Word Radiocommunication Conference 2023 (WRC-23), this document provides possible solutions in order to preserve in the future the Sea Surface Temperature (SST) measurement in the microwave domain. The potential solutions depicted in that document are only based on a frequency sharing with incumbent services and would have to be studied in terms of SST measurement capabilities.

articleTitle: Measuring receiver noise parameters for global 21-cm experiments
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: Radiometer experiments to detect 21-cm Hydrogen line emission from the Cosmic Dawn and Epoch of Reionization rely upon precise absolute calibration. Noise generated by amplifiers within the radiometer receiver must be accounted for; however, it is difficult to measure as the noise power varies with source impedance. In this letter, we introduce a convenient method to measure the noise parameters of a receiver system, which is practical for low-frequency receivers used in global 21-cm experiments.

articleTitle: A 400 W Continuous Wave Power Amplifier in L-Band with single GaN Transistor
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper presents the design, manufacturing and testing of a continuous-wave 400 W Power amplifier in L-Band. The device is based on a single GaN high power transistor mounted in a connectorized module. The amplifier demonstrates an output power higher than 400 W at 3 dB compression. This is the highest power achieved by a single device amplifier reported on L-Band to date. Moreover, the measured gain is 15 dB and PAE is 72%.

articleTitle: Long-Term Reliability of PDN Design Based on Decap Aging and Temperature
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The Power Delivery Network (PDN) of an electronic system in a data center is an important design portion that ensure the proper current supply and functionality of the active components. Its performances are affected by the temperature and aging of the PDN components, mainly the decoupling capacitors, thus the long-term reliability of the PDN requires high-level of attention to be able to predict how much its performances differ from the nominal design. A realistic test case is analyzed in this paper and a statistical prediction methodology is developed to effectively dealing with the long-term PDN degradation.

articleTitle: Waveguide-Floquet Mapping Based on Surface Susceptibilities for Metasurface Unit Cell Characterization
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: A simple method is proposed to characterize metasurface unit cells using rectangular waveguide. The method maps the S-parameters obtained using a dominant-mode waveguide to the S-parameters of fundamental Floquet mode for a plane wave incident at any desired angle. The mapping between the dominant waveguide mode and the fundamental Floquet mode is executed by extracting the equivalent surface susceptibilities of the metasurface unit cell. The results obtained from the proposed method show good agreement with the full-wave simulation results of the metasurface unit cell.

articleTitle: A Dual Polarized Shared Aperture Compact Unit Cell Element for Antenna Array Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: A dual polarized compact unit cell antenna element is presented for shared aperture antenna arrays. The unit cell is composed of two linearly polarized antennas sharing the same aperture both operating at the same frequency band. The unit element has about % 7.06 bandwidth (VSWR<1.22) and the isolation between each antenna in the unit cell is more than -43 dB. The unit cell element has cross polarization level better than -40 dB in the principle plane. The unit cell is composed of full metal to have only metallic losses. The proposed unit cell spacing is about 0.885λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> at the center frequency to prevent grating lobes in the band. The proposed unit cell structure allows compact construction of the feed network for array antenna applications.

articleTitle: Optimization identification algorithm of characteristic parameters of electromagnetic emission elements
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: It is very difficult to analyze electromagnetic interference in complex electronic information systems because of the wide range of internal and external electromagnetic environment and the complex coupling relationship. Electromagnetic emission can be characterized and analyzed by the theory of electromagnetic emission elements. Harmonics are an important part of many types of electromagnetic emission and can be considered as the key to identify most basic elements of switch class. However, most electromagnetic emission test data are noisy signals, which greatly reduces the accuracy of switch element identification. In this paper, starting from the electromagnetic emission test data, the electromagnetic emission spectrum data is processed in time domain, and then the compressed sensing method is used to improve the signal-to-noise ratio of the data, so as to improve the accuracy of extracting, identifying and characterizing the basic elements of switch class and the parameters in time domain and frequency domain from the test data.

articleTitle: Modified Wheeler cap method using a quarter-wave transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: The Wheeler cap method was used to measure the radiation efficiency of antennas. The conventional method introduces errors in the measurement of radiation efficiency because a small loss resistance is difficult to measure. In this study, we propose a method that combines the Wheeler cap method with a quarter-wave transformer (QWT). The QWT is connected to the antenna to transform its impedance. Numerical validation confirmed that impedance transformation using QWT can transform a small loss resistance to a reasonable value. This would allow the proposed method to measure the radiation efficiency with a better accuracy.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Disturbance Issues in 400 MHz Wireless Medical Telemetry Systems and Its Countermeasures for Safety Operation
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: A wireless medical telemetry system (WMTS) is typical medical device that use radio communications and monitor various biological parameters. In Japan, the frequency band of 400 MHz is allocated for WMTS. However, the issues that cause poor reception of WMTS are considerable concern. For example, 400 MHz frequency band is also shared for other radio communication systems. It has been reported that passive intermodulation effect is fatal poor reception effects on WMTS. Additionally, the electromagnetic noises generated from switched-mode power supply, especially installed in light-emitting diode (LED) lamp and can reach over 400 MHz frequency band. In this study, we observed the potential of electromagnetic disturbance in communication+ in WMTS caused by other radio communication systems, an effect of passive intermodulation and noises generated from LED lamp and discussed countermeasures for this serious issue.

articleTitle: Multisection 3-dB Ultra-Broadband Directional Coupler Composed of Coupled-Line Sections Designed in PCB and MMIC Technologies
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: In this paper, we present a new 3-dB ultra-broadband directional coupler with bandwidth exceeding one frequency decade. The proposed topology is composed of three coupled-line sections and two transmission lines having unequal lengths. In comparison to the known solutions, the proposed approach requires weaker coupling of coupled-line sections which makes it easier to implement in technologies where the achievement of a strong coupling is not possible due to physical constrains. The ultra-broadband directional coupler has been designed in PCB and monolithic technologies as components operating at 1 GHz and 20 GHz center frequency, respectively. The obtained measurements and electromagnetic simulations feature good electrical properties of the developed designs and confirm applicability of the proposed concept.

articleTitle: Development of Commercial and Defense Microwave and Laser Directed Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: We shall address shortly the origin and principles of Directed Energy Systems (DES). Nicolas Tesla, the genius in electro-magnetism, tried to transmit wireless electrical energy instead of using wires or cables, first implemented and patented DES at the beginning of the 20 century, but he failed to implement DES because the technology was not yet mature. In the same period, the development of wireless communication systems by Marconi, Popov, and other professionals had a big success and became one of the most important technologic fields. Power and efficiency limitations, Electro Magnetic Interference (EMI), and biohazardous effects all have delayed the development of DES for more than 70 years. This summary paper presents a short review of the past, present, and future of DES.

articleTitle: Investigation of Range-Correlated Features in Fourier Domain Artifacts Measured Using a Dynamic Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: We investigate range-dependent artifacts manifesting in the Fourier domain responses of conductive cylinder measured with a two-element interferometric dynamic antenna array. By illuminating the scene with two noise transmitters and capturing the scattered signals at two receiving antennas, angle-dependent spatial frequency (two-dimensional Fourier domain) responses of the scene can be obtained via rotational array dynamics. Finite bandwidth signals exhibit range correlation, which manifests in range-dependent measurements. For long conducting objects, the projected baseline changes as a function of rotation angle, causing appreciable range and thus phase variations. We explore cyclical responses manifesting as a function of angle and target range for potential use in target range estimation.
